kurs:e01.titel: The EPC provision by provision (EQE Paper D)
kurs:e01.untertitel: The provisions Paper D asks about most often: from Art. 14 EPC to Art. 153 EPC, with case law, Guidelines and Official Journal
kurs:e01.beschreibung: One chapter per provision, in EPC order and selected by frequency in the legal questions of the EQE (Paper D 2015 to 2025): languages, right to the patent, divisional applications, date of filing, renewal fees, priority, novelty, examination and grant, opposition, limitation, appeal, time limits, further processing, re-establishment of rights, amendments, representation, Euro-PCT and the international phase. Each case is short facts with several questions; flashcards show, for every article and rule, the decisions of the Boards of Appeal, the sections of the Guidelines and the notices in the Official Journal.

kapitel:e01n14.titel: Art. 14 EPC, R. 3 and 6 EPC: languages and translations

einheit:e01n14-0.text: An application may be filed with the EPO in **any language**; the translation into an official language follows within two months (Art. 14(2) EPC, R. 6(1) EPC) and determines the **language of the proceedings** (Art. 14(3) EPC). Paper D asks about this in many variants: correcting an erroneous translation (2015), the language reduction for a Portuguese university (2017), a divisional application in the wrong language (2021), the language of a PCT application (2024) and an opposition in Spanish under Art. 14(4) EPC (2024). Points to remember: translation time limits are excluded from further processing, and the language of the proceedings cannot be changed (G 4/08).

gruppe:e01n14-1.sachverhalt: N. K., based in Osaka, files a European application in Japanese with the EPO on Monday, 9 March 2026, without claiming priority. An English translation is to follow later.

einheit:e01n14-1a.frage: Does the application obtain a date of filing although it is not in an official language of the EPO?
loesung: **Yes.** A European application may be filed in any language (Art. 14(2) EPC). Language is not a requirement for a date of filing (R. 40(1) EPC); the translation is only required in the examination as to formal requirements (R. 57 EPC).
einheit:e01n14-1a.merke: Any language secures the date of filing.
einheit:e01n14-1a.abschnitt: Art. 14(2) and 14(3) EPC: filing, translation, language of the proceedings

einheit:e01n14-1b.frage: By when must N. K. file the translation?
loesung: **By 11 May 2026.** The time limit is two months after filing the application (R. 6(1) EPC) and would expire on Saturday, 9 May 2026 (R. 131(4) EPC). It is extended to the next day on which the EPO is open for receipt of documents (R. 134(1) EPC).
einheit:e01n14-1b.abschnitt: Art. 14(2) and 14(3) EPC: filing, translation, language of the proceedings

einheit:e01n14-1c.frage: N. K. misses the time limit and also the two months set in the invitation under R. 58 EPC. Can she request further processing?
loesung: **No.** The application is deemed to be withdrawn (third sentence of Art. 14(2) EPC). The time limits under R. 6(1) EPC and R. 58 EPC are excluded from further processing (R. 135(2) EPC). Re-establishment of rights in respect of the time limit under R. 58 EPC remains possible (Art. 122 EPC; Guidelines A-III, 14).
einheit:e01n14-1c.abschnitt: Art. 14(2) and 14(3) EPC: filing, translation, language of the proceedings

einheit:e01n14-1d.frage: N. K. files the English translation in time. May she later file amended claims in German?
loesung: **No.** With the translation, English has become the language of the proceedings (Art. 14(3) EPC). Amendments to the application must be filed in the language of the proceedings (R. 3(2) EPC). Other submissions may be in any official language (R. 3(1) EPC).
einheit:e01n14-1d.merke: Amendments only in the language of the proceedings.
einheit:e01n14-1d.abschnitt: Art. 14(2) and 14(3) EPC: filing, translation, language of the proceedings

gruppe:e01n14-2.sachverhalt: L files EP-L1 in Korean with an English translation filed in time, and EP-L2 directly in English. Both English texts read “5 mm” in claim 1; the Korean text of EP-L1 and the Korean priority application read “5 µm”. The error cannot be recognised from the English texts alone.

einheit:e01n14-2a.frage: Can L replace “mm” with “µm” in EP-L1?
loesung: **Yes.** Throughout the proceedings, the translation may be brought into conformity with the application as filed (second sentence of Art. 14(2) EPC). The application as filed is the Korean text (Art. 70(2) EPC); it reads “5 µm”, so the correction adds nothing.
einheit:e01n14-2a.merke: Filed in a non-official language: the original is the yardstick.
einheit:e01n14-2a.abschnitt: Art. 14(2) EPC: translation and application as filed

einheit:e01n14-2b.frage: Can L correct the error in EP-L2 under R. 139 EPC by referring to the priority application?
loesung: **No.** EP-L2 was filed in English; the English text is the application as filed. For claims, the error and the correction must be immediately evident from the documents as filed (R. 139 EPC, G 3/89); priority documents may not be used for this (Guidelines H-VI, 2.2.1). Here the error is not recognisable.
einheit:e01n14-2b.merke: Priority documents do not help under R. 139 EPC.
einheit:e01n14-2b.abschnitt: Art. 14(2) EPC: translation and application as filed

gruppe:e01n14-3.sachverhalt: The US company Q files an international application in German; it is published in German. On entry into the European phase, Q wishes to conduct the proceedings before the EPO in English.

einheit:e01n14-3a.frage: Can Q file an English translation on entry and thereby make English the language of the proceedings?
loesung: **No.** If the international application was filed and published in an official language of the EPO, that language remains the language of the proceedings; a translation into another official language is not possible (G 4/08, Art. 14(3) EPC). In written proceedings, the EPO uses only the language of the proceedings.
einheit:e01n14-3a.merke: The language of the proceedings cannot be changed.
einheit:e01n14-3a.abschnitt: Art. 14(3) EPC: language of the proceedings

einheit:e01n14-3b.frage: May Q write its replies to communications in English?
loesung: **Yes.** In written proceedings, any party may use any official language of the EPO (R. 3(1) EPC). However, Q must file amended claims and description pages in German (R. 3(2) EPC).
einheit:e01n14-3b.merke: Submissions in any official language, amendments in the language of the proceedings.
einheit:e01n14-3b.abschnitt: Art. 14(3) EPC: language of the proceedings

gruppe:e01n14-4.sachverhalt: The opposition period against patent EP-P (language of the proceedings German) expires on Monday, 14 September 2026. On 3 August 2026, M, an Italian national resident in Munich, and O S.r.l., based in Milan, jointly file an opposition in Italian and pay the fee.

einheit:e01n14-4a.frage: Were M and O allowed to file the opposition in Italian?
loesung: **Yes.** Persons with their principal place of business in a Contracting State whose official language is not English, French or German (O in Italy), and nationals of that State resident abroad (M), may file documents subject to a time limit in an official language of that State (first sentence of Art. 14(4) EPC).
einheit:e01n14-4a.merke: Admissible non-official language: seat in the State or its nationality suffices.

einheit:e01n14-4b.frage: By when must the translation be received?
optionen: Two months after an invitation from the EPO
loesung: **By 14 September 2026.** In principle, the time limit is one month after filing the document (first sentence of R. 6(2) EPC), here 3 September 2026. For an opposition, filing by the end of the opposition period suffices if that period expires later (third sentence of R. 6(2) EPC).
einheit:e01n14-4b.merke: Opposition: translation by the end of the opposition period if that ends later.

einheit:e01n14-4c.frage: Must the translation be in German, the language of the proceedings?
loesung: **No.** The translation under Art. 14(4) EPC may be filed in any official language of the EPO (second sentence of R. 3(1) EPC), so also in English or French.

einheit:e01n14-4d.frage: Has the opposition then been validly filed?
loesung: **No.** If a required translation is not filed in due time, the document is deemed not to have been filed (third sentence of Art. 14(4) EPC). Further processing is available only to the applicant (Art. 121(1) EPC), and the opposition period has expired.
einheit:e01n14-4d.merke: Translation too late: opposition deemed not filed.
einheit:e01n14-4d.abwandlung: The translation is not received until 15 September 2026.

gruppe:e01n14-5.sachverhalt: University U, based in Porto, has never filed a European application. It wants to file an invention whose description exists in Portuguese; an English translation is ready. U wants to pay as little in fees as possible.

einheit:e01n14-5a.frage: How does U obtain the language reduction of the filing fee?
optionen: File the application in English and declare that it is a university
File only the request for grant in Portuguese
File at least the description in Portuguese, the translation not earlier, and declare its status
File the Portuguese version after the English one
loesung: **Description in Portuguese, translation not earlier, declaration.** The reduction requires filing in an admissible non-official language (R. 7a(1) EPC, Art. 14(1) RFees); what counts is the description, not the request for grant (Guidelines A-X, 9.3.2). Universities are entitled (R. 7a(2) EPC); U must expressly declare its status.
einheit:e01n14-5a.merke: Language reduction: description in the admissible non-official language.

einheit:e01n14-5b.frage: Is the search fee also reduced under the language arrangements?
loesung: **No.** R. 7a(1) EPC reduces only the filing and examination fees. But U obtains the micro-entity reduction, which also covers the search fee (R. 7a(3) EPC): universities qualify, and U has not filed five applications in five years (R. 7a(4) EPC). Both reductions are applied successively (Guidelines A-X, 9.2).
einheit:e01n14-5b.merke: Language arrangements: filing and examination fees; micro-entities: also search, designation, grant and renewal fees.

einheit:e01n14-5c.frage: Does the enterprise obtain a reduction of the search fee?
loesung: **No.** As a small or medium-sized enterprise, it obtains only the language reduction (R. 7a(2) EPC). R. 7a(3) EPC applies only to micro-enterprises, natural persons, non-profit organisations, universities and public research organisations; other SMEs are excluded (Guidelines A-X, 9.4.1).
einheit:e01n14-5c.merke: SMEs that are not micro-enterprises: language reduction only.
einheit:e01n14-5c.abwandlung: Instead of U, the applicant is a Portuguese company with 120 employees.

kapitel:e01n51.titel: Art. 51 EPC and RFees: paying, reducing and refunding fees

einheit:e01n51-0.titel: When is a fee paid, what is reduced, what comes back?
einheit:e01n51-0.text: Art. 51 EPC allows the EPO to levy fees; their amount and the method of payment are laid down in the Rules relating to Fees (Art. 51(4) EPC). Paper D asks about them in case scenarios: 2017 (language reduction for a university, empty deposit account), 2019 (account replenished too late), 2021 (refund of search and examination fees) and 2025 (automatic debiting). Older model answers are partly outdated: since 1 April 2024 the reductions are in **R. 7a EPC**, with a new scheme for micro-enterprises; for bank transfers there is no longer a surcharge for orders given in the last ten days (Art. 7(3) RFees); deposit accounts have their own fail-safe provision (Guidelines A-X, 6.2.2).

gruppe:e01n51-1.titel: The transfer on the last day
gruppe:e01n51-1.sachverhalt: The time limit for N's examination fee expires on Monday, 14 September 2026. On 14 September 2026, N instructs his bank in Vienna to make the transfer. The amount is credited to the EPO's account on 16 September 2026.

einheit:e01n51-1a.frage: Which day is in principle considered the date of payment?
optionen: 14 September 2026, the day of the order
15 September 2026, the day N's account is debited
16 September 2026, the day the EPO's account is credited
The day on which the EPO books the payment
loesung: **16 September 2026.** The date of payment is the date on which the amount is credited to a bank account held by the EPO (Art. 7(1) RFees). Bank transfer is the basic method (Art. 5(1) RFees); alongside it are deposit account, credit card and transfer of a refund (Guidelines A-X, 2).
einheit:e01n51-1a.merke: A fee is paid when the money reaches the EPO's account.

einheit:e01n51-1b.frage: Is the time limit nevertheless deemed observed?
loesung: **Yes.** The time limit is deemed observed if N provides evidence that, within the period, he duly gave the transfer order in a Contracting State (Art. 7(3) RFees); the EPO may request this evidence (Art. 7(4) RFees). There is no longer a surcharge for orders given in the last ten days of the period.
einheit:e01n51-1b.merke: An order to a bank in a Contracting State within the period suffices.

einheit:e01n51-1c.frage: Is the time limit deemed observed in this case too?
loesung: **No.** Art. 7(3) RFees requires the order to be given in a Contracting State. With the credit on 16 September 2026 the time limit is missed; the application is deemed to be withdrawn (Art. 94(2) EPC). N can still request further processing (Art. 121 EPC).
einheit:e01n51-1c.merke: Bank order outside the Contracting States: no fail-safe.
einheit:e01n51-1c.abwandlung: N gives the order on 14 September 2026 at his bank in New York.

gruppe:e01n51-2.sachverhalt: O has issued an automatic debit order for his application from his deposit account with the EPO. On 13 November 2026, the last day for the examination fee, the account has insufficient funds. On 12 November 2026, O had initiated a SEPA transfer to replenish it; it is credited on 16 November 2026.

einheit:e01n51-2a.frage: Is the examination fee deemed paid on 13 November 2026?
loesung: **No.** If the balance is insufficient, payment is deemed made only on the day the account is sufficiently replenished, here 16 November 2026 (Guidelines A-X, 4.2.4). Until then, no further debit orders are executed either.
einheit:e01n51-2a.merke: Insufficient funds: paid only on replenishment.
einheit:e01n51-2a.abschnitt: Art. 5 RFees: deposit account and automatic debiting

einheit:e01n51-2b.frage: Can O nevertheless save the time limit without further processing?
loesung: **Yes,** through the fail-safe provision for deposit accounts: the time limit is deemed observed if O proves that he initiated the replenishment by SEPA transfer at least one day before the time limit expired (Guidelines A-X, 6.2.2). After a communication noting a loss of rights, O requests a decision under R. 112(2) EPC and, in the alternative, further processing (Guidelines A-X, 6.2.5).
einheit:e01n51-2b.merke: SEPA one day before, SEPA Instant on the last day, otherwise three days before.
einheit:e01n51-2b.abschnitt: Art. 5 RFees: deposit account and automatic debiting

einheit:e01n51-2c.frage: Can O limit the automatic debit order to the examination fee?
loesung: **No.** An automatic debit order covers all fees of its type in the proceedings and cannot be limited to individual fees. There are only three types: all fees, all fees except renewal fees, or renewal fees only (Guidelines A-X, 4.3).
einheit:e01n51-2c.merke: Automatic debiting: all or nothing per type.
einheit:e01n51-2c.abschnitt: Art. 5 RFees: deposit account and automatic debiting

gruppe:e01n51-3.sachverhalt: A Portuguese university H wants to file a European application claiming the priority of its Portuguese application. An English translation is available. In the preceding five years, H filed two European applications.

einheit:e01n51-3a.frage: Does H obtain the reduction of the filing fee if it files the application directly in English?
loesung: **No.** The language reduction under R. 7a(1) EPC requires the application, at least the description, to be filed in an admissible non-official language (Guidelines A-X, 9.3.2). H files in Portuguese and the English translation afterwards or at the same time, not earlier (Guidelines A-X, 9.3.1).
einheit:e01n51-3a.merke: Language reduction only when filing in one's own non-official language.

einheit:e01n51-3b.frage: Can H also pay a reduced search fee?
loesung: **Yes,** but not because of the language: R. 7a(1) EPC concerns only the filing and examination fees. As a university with fewer than five applications in five years, H also falls under R. 7a(3) EPC and R. 7a(4) EPC; this 30 % reduction also covers the search fee (Art. 14(1) RFees).

einheit:e01n51-3c.frage: Are both reductions applied together to the filing fee?
loesung: **Yes.** Where several reductions apply to the same fee, they are calculated successively (Art. 14(3) RFees; Guidelines A-X, 9.2). H must declare that it is entitled at the latest with the first reduced payment (R. 7b(1) EPC).
einheit:e01n51-3c.merke: Several reductions: successively, declaration with the first payment.

gruppe:e01n51-4.sachverhalt: Q Inc., based in Boston, has eight employees and an annual turnover of EUR 1 million. It files a European application in English; in the preceding five years it filed two European applications.

einheit:e01n51-4a.frage: Can Q obtain fee reductions despite being based in the USA?
loesung: **Yes.** The reduction for micro-enterprises, natural persons, universities and similar entities under R. 7a(3) EPC applies irrespective of nationality and seat (Guidelines A-X, 9.4.1). With fewer than ten employees and a turnover of no more than EUR 2 million, Q is a micro-enterprise.
einheit:e01n51-4a.merke: Micro-entities worldwide, language reduction only for Europe.

einheit:e01n51-4b.frage: Is the renewal fee for the application also reduced?
loesung: **Yes.** R. 7a(3) EPC covers the filing, search, examination, designation and grant fees and the renewal fees for European patent applications, each by 30 % (Art. 14(1) RFees). A medium-sized enterprise that is not a micro-enterprise does not obtain this reduction.
einheit:e01n51-4b.merke: Six fees, including the renewal fees for the application.

loesung: **No.** Anyone who has filed five or more European or Euro-PCT applications within the five years before the date of filing is excluded (R. 7a(4) EPC). If Q has already paid a reduced fee, the EPO invites it to pay the shortfall within two months (Guidelines A-X, 9.4.3).
einheit:e01n51-4c.merke: Five applications in five years end the reduction.
einheit:e01n51-4c.abwandlung: In the five years before the date of filing, Q has filed five European applications.

gruppe:e01n51-5.titel: Two applications nobody wants any more
gruppe:e01n51-5.sachverhalt: R paid the search and examination fees for EP-1 and EP-2 on filing. For EP-1, the EPO invites R under R. 58 EPC to file claims; the search has not begun. For EP-2, R waived the invitation under R. 70(2) EPC; a first communication from the Examining Division came with the search report.

einheit:e01n51-5a.frage: Does R get the search fee back in full if EP-1 is withdrawn?
loesung: **Yes.** The search fee is refunded in full if the application is withdrawn before the EPO has begun to draw up the search report (Art. 9(1) RFees). Form 1704 in the file shows when the search began (Guidelines A-X, 10.2.1).
einheit:e01n51-5a.merke: Search not begun: search fee refunded in full.

einheit:e01n51-5b.frage: Does R also get the examination fee for EP-1 back in full?
loesung: **Yes.** If the application is withdrawn, refused or deemed to be withdrawn before substantive examination has begun, the examination fee is refunded in full (Art. 11(a) RFees; Guidelines A-VI, 2.5).
einheit:e01n51-5b.merke: Before substantive examination: examination fee refunded in full.

einheit:e01n51-5c.frage: Can R still get any fees back for EP-2?
loesung: **Yes,** half of the examination fee, if R withdraws EP-2 before expiry of the time limit for replying to the first communication of the Examining Division under Art. 94(3) EPC (Art. 11(b) RFees). The EPO keeps the search fee because the search has been carried out (Art. 9(1) RFees).
einheit:e01n51-5c.merke: After substantive examination has begun: 50 % until the first time limit for reply expires.

einheit:e01n51-5d.frage: May R make a withdrawal conditional on a full refund of the examination fee?
loesung: **Yes.** An applicant unsure whether substantive examination has begun may withdraw the application on condition of a full refund (Guidelines A-VI, 2.5). Form 2095 in the file shows that substantive examination has begun.
einheit:e01n51-5d.merke: Conditional withdrawal secures the full refund.

kapitel:e01n54.titel: Art. 54 and 55 EPC: novelty and state of the art

einheit:e01n54-0.text: Art. 54 EPC is the provision relied on most often in Paper D (15 of the 54 questions from 2015 to 2025). The question is almost never whether a document discloses the invention, but **whether it is state of the art at all**. To answer it, first determine the effective date of each claim (priority, Art. 89 EPC), then classify each document: published earlier under **Art. 54(2) EPC**, earlier European application under **Art. 54(3) EPC** (novelty only) or no state of the art at all. Art. 55 EPC excludes abuse and recognised exhibitions, not one's own publications.

einheit:e01n54-0s.titel: Examination scheme: state of the art

gruppe:e01n54-1.titel: The journal article in the priority interval
gruppe:e01n54-1.sachverhalt: A files a German application for process X on 3 March 2025 and publishes a journal article on X on 2 June 2025. On 3 March 2026, A files a European application claiming the German priority. Claim 1 relates to X, claim 2 to X with feature Y, which only the European application describes.

einheit:e01n54-1a.frage: Is the journal article state of the art for claim 1?
loesung: **No.** Claim 1 enjoys the priority of 3 March 2025: first application, same invention, twelve-month period observed (Art. 87(1) EPC). The priority date counts as the date of filing (Art. 89 EPC); the article of 2 June 2025 appeared later.
einheit:e01n54-1a.merke: Valid priority moves the relevant date to the priority date.
einheit:e01n54-1a.abschnitt: Art. 54(2) EPC: prior-published state of the art

einheit:e01n54-1b.frage: Is the journal article state of the art under Art. 54(2) EPC for claim 2?
loesung: **Yes.** X with Y is not disclosed in the German application; for claim 2 the date of filing, 3 March 2026, applies (G 2/98). The article was made available to the public before then, so it is state of the art for novelty and inventive step (G 3/93).
einheit:e01n54-1b.merke: Without priority, even one's own publication in the interval is prejudicial.
einheit:e01n54-1b.abschnitt: Art. 54(2) EPC: prior-published state of the art

einheit:e01n54-1c.frage: Can A rely on Art. 55 EPC for claim 2?
loesung: **No.** Art. 55(1) EPC covers only evident abuse and display at recognised exhibitions. One's own publication does not fall under it; moreover, it took place more than six months before filing (G 3/98).
einheit:e01n54-1c.merke: The EPC has no grace period for one's own publications.
einheit:e01n54-1c.abschnitt: Art. 54(2) EPC: prior-published state of the art

gruppe:e01n54-2.sachverhalt: B files European application EP-B on 10 January 2025; the description discloses X, the claims relate to Z. EP-B is published on 10 July 2026. On 5 May 2025, A files EP-A, without priority, with a claim to X.

einheit:e01n54-2a.frage: Is EP-B state of the art for EP-A?
loesung: **Yes,** under Art. 54(3) EPC: EP-B was filed before the date of filing of EP-A and published afterwards. What counts is the **whole content** as filed, so the description as well.
einheit:e01n54-2a.merke: Art. 54(3) EPC: whole content as filed, not just the claims.

einheit:e01n54-2b.frage: Can EP-B also be raised against the inventive step of EP-A?
loesung: **No.** Prior rights under Art. 54(3) EPC are not considered in deciding whether there has been an inventive step (second sentence of Art. 56 EPC).

einheit:e01n54-2c.frage: May A restore novelty with a disclaimer not disclosed in the application?
loesung: **Yes.** Under G 1/03, an undisclosed disclaimer is allowable to delimit a claim against state of the art under Art. 54(3) EPC; it may not exclude more than necessary and must not make a technical contribution (G 1/16).
einheit:e01n54-2c.merke: Against Art. 54(3) EPC, an undisclosed disclaimer helps.

einheit:e01n54-2d.frage: Is EP-B still state of the art if B withdraws the application in time for it never to be published?
loesung: **No.** Art. 54(3) EPC requires the earlier application to have been **published** on or after the date of filing. Without publication, there is no prior right.
einheit:e01n54-2d.abwandlung: B withdraws EP-B before the technical preparations for publication have been completed.

gruppe:e01n54-3.titel: The PCT application that never came to Europe
gruppe:e01n54-3.sachverhalt: On 1 February 2024, C files international application PCT-C, which discloses X; it is published in English on 1 August 2025. C performs none of the acts under R. 159 EPC. On 1 March 2024, A files a European application with a claim to X.

einheit:e01n54-3a.frage: Is PCT-C state of the art under Art. 54(3) EPC for A's application?
loesung: **No.** A Euro-PCT application is considered state of the art under Art. 54(3) EPC only if the filing fee has been paid and, where required, the translation filed (Art. 153(5) EPC, R. 165 EPC). C has done neither.
einheit:e01n54-3a.merke: Euro-PCT as prior right only with the filing fee (R. 165 EPC).

einheit:e01n54-3b.frage: Is the publication of PCT-C of 1 August 2025 state of the art under Art. 54(2) EPC?
loesung: **No.** It appeared after A's date of filing (1 March 2024). Art. 54(2) EPC covers only what was made available to the public **before** the relevant date.
einheit:e01n54-3b.merke: Published after the relevant date: relevant only via Art. 54(3) EPC.

einheit:e01n54-3c.frage: Does this change if C pays the filing fee under R. 159(1) EPC?
loesung: **Yes.** With the filing fee (no translation needed, as it is in English), the requirements of R. 165 EPC are met; PCT-C retroactively becomes a prior right under Art. 54(3) EPC against A's application.
einheit:e01n54-3c.merke: Entry into the European phase makes the PCT application a prior right.
einheit:e01n54-3c.abwandlung: C enters the European phase in due time and pays the filing fee.

gruppe:e01n54-4.titel: The sealing material on the market
gruppe:e01n54-4.sachverhalt: Since 2020, D has been selling a sealing material for solar modules. Its composition cannot be fully analysed or reproduced with the means available before the date of filing. In 2023, E files an application for exactly this composition and argues that the product is not part of the state of the art.

einheit:e01n54-4a.frage: Is the product sold part of the state of the art although it was not reproducible?
loesung: **Yes.** A product put on the market before the date of filing cannot be excluded from the state of the art merely because the skilled person could not analyse and reproduce its composition (G 1/23, clarifying G 1/92).
einheit:e01n54-4a.merke: Sold means made available to the public – even without reproducibility.
einheit:e01n54-4a.abschnitt: Art. 54(2) EPC: availability to the public

einheit:e01n54-4b.frage: Are the publicly available data sheets of the product also part of the state of the art?
loesung: **Yes.** Technical information about the product that was made available to the public before the date of filing is state of the art, irrespective of whether the product itself could be analysed (G 1/23).
einheit:e01n54-4b.merke: Information about the product counts too.
einheit:e01n54-4b.abschnitt: Art. 54(2) EPC: availability to the public

gruppe:e01n54-5.titel: Once a week instead of daily
gruppe:e01n54-5.sachverhalt: Active substance W is known for treating disease K at 10 mg daily. F discovers that 50 mg once a week is better tolerated in K and wants to protect this.

einheit:e01n54-5a.frage: Can F obtain a claim to W for use in K with the new dosage, although the substance and the disease are known?
loesung: **Yes.** Art. 54(5) EPC does not exclude protection of a known medicament for a **different therapeutic treatment of the same disease**; novelty may lie solely in a dosage regime (G 2/08).
einheit:e01n54-5a.merke: A new dosage can be a further medical use.

einheit:e01n54-5b.frage: May F draft the claim in Swiss-type form (“Use of W for the manufacture of a medicament for the treatment of K”)?
loesung: **No.** Where novelty is conferred only by the new therapeutic use, the Swiss-type claim format is no longer allowable since G 2/08; the correct form is the purpose-limited product claim “W for use in …” (Art. 54(5) EPC).
einheit:e01n54-5b.merke: Purpose-limited product claim instead of Swiss-type.

kapitel:e01n61.titel: Art. 60 and 61 EPC, R. 14 to 16 EPC: right to the patent

einheit:e01n61-0.text: The right to the patent is decided not by the EPO but by a national court; before the EPO, the applicant is deemed entitled (Art. 60(3) EPC). The EPC nevertheless protects the true owner: if they prove their action, the grant proceedings are **stayed** (R. 14(1) EPC), time limits other than those for renewal fees are interrupted (R. 14(4) EPC), and the applicant may not withdraw (R. 15 EPC). After a final decision, the entitled person has **three months** for the remedies of Art. 61(1) EPC (R. 16(1) EPC). Paper D 2019 tested the whole chain, up to the divisional application after resumption of the proceedings.

gruppe:e01n61-1.sachverhalt: In 2024, J brings an action before a national court against the applicant K, claiming entitlement to the grant; the EPO stays the grant proceedings on 3 June 2024. The court proceedings are still pending in 2026. K presses for grant.

einheit:e01n61-1a.frage: Can the EPO itself decide whether K or J is entitled?
loesung: **No.** In proceedings before the EPO, the applicant is deemed entitled to exercise the right to the patent (Art. 60(3) EPC). Entitlement to the grant is decided by the national courts; their decisions are recognised under the Protocol on Recognition, which is an integral part of the Convention (Art. 164(1) EPC).
einheit:e01n61-1a.merke: The EPO does not examine entitlement.
einheit:e01n61-1a.abschnitt: Art. 60(3) EPC, R. 14(3) and 14(4) EPC: entitlement and resumption

einheit:e01n61-1b.frage: Must the EPO wait for the end of the court proceedings before resuming?
loesung: **No.** The EPO may set a date on which it intends to resume the grant proceedings regardless of the stage reached in the national proceedings. If no final decision has been proven by then, it may resume (R. 14(3) EPC).
einheit:e01n61-1b.merke: The EPO need not wait indefinitely.
einheit:e01n61-1b.abschnitt: Art. 60(3) EPC, R. 14(3) and 14(4) EPC: entitlement and resumption

einheit:e01n61-1c.frage: When the proceedings were stayed, three weeks of the period for requesting examination remained. Does K have only three weeks after resumption?
loesung: **No.** The part of the time limit not yet elapsed begins to run on the date of resumption; however, the remaining period is at least two months (R. 14(4) EPC).
einheit:e01n61-1c.merke: After resumption, at least two months remain.
einheit:e01n61-1c.abschnitt: Art. 60(3) EPC, R. 14(3) and 14(4) EPC: entitlement and resumption

gruppe:e01n61-2.sachverhalt: A's application EP-A has been published. On 5 October 2026, the Examining Division issues the communication under R. 71(3) EPC. B has sued A before a competent German court to obtain entitlement to the grant. On 26 October 2026, B files proof of the action with the EPO.

einheit:e01n61-2a.frage: Are the grant proceedings stayed although A objects?
loesung: **Yes.** If a third party proves that it has opened proceedings seeking a decision under Art. 61(1) EPC, the proceedings are stayed (R. 14(1) EPC); only B could consent to their continuation. The application has been published, and the proof precedes the mention of grant (J 14/19).
einheit:e01n61-2a.merke: Stay: proof of action, after publication, before the mention of grant.

einheit:e01n61-2b.frage: Does the time limit under R. 71(3) EPC continue to run during the stay?
loesung: **No.** All time limits running on the date of the stay are interrupted; after resumption the remainder runs, but at least two months (R. 14(4) EPC). The stay takes effect on receipt of the proof, here from 26 October 2026 (Guidelines A-IV, 2.2.2).
einheit:e01n61-2b.merke: Interrupted, not restarted: rest of the period, at least two months.

einheit:e01n61-2c.frage: Must renewal fees be paid during the stay?
loesung: **Yes.** The time limits for paying renewal fees are exempt from the interruption (R. 14(4) EPC). If A does not pay, B should; anyone may validly pay fees (Guidelines A-X, 1). Otherwise the application is deemed to be withdrawn (Art. 86(1) EPC).
einheit:e01n61-2c.merke: Renewal fees continue to fall due despite the stay.

einheit:e01n61-2d.frage: Can A withdraw the application during the stay to deprive B of the proceedings?
loesung: **No.** From the date on which the third party proves the action until the proceedings are resumed, neither the application nor the designation of any Contracting State may be withdrawn (R. 15 EPC).

gruppe:e01n61-3.titel: The divisional application during the stay
gruppe:e01n61-3.sachverhalt: G's application EP-G describes inventions X and Y and claims X. On 4 May 2026, H proves to the EPO that he has brought an action for entitlement to the grant. On 12 May 2026, G files a divisional application for Y; G receives the communication of the stay only on 20 May 2026.

einheit:e01n61-3a.frage: Has the divisional application been validly filed?
loesung: **No.** The stay takes effect on receipt of the proof, here from 4 May 2026, even if G receives the communication later (J 9/12). During the stay the status quo is preserved; a divisional application cannot be filed (J 20/05; Guidelines A-IV, 2.2.3).
einheit:e01n61-3a.merke: The stay bars divisional applications from receipt of the proof.
einheit:e01n61-3a.abschnitt: R. 14 EPC: effects of the stay

einheit:e01n61-3b.frage: H wins by final decision and prosecutes EP-G under Art. 61(1)(a) EPC. Can H file the divisional application for Y after resumption?
loesung: **Yes.** With the declaration under Art. 61(1)(a) EPC, H takes G's place. As applicant, H can file a divisional application on the resumed, pending application (R. 36(1) EPC); G can no longer do so.
einheit:e01n61-3b.merke: After resumption, the new applicant divides.
einheit:e01n61-3b.abschnitt: R. 14 EPC: effects of the stay

gruppe:e01n61-4.sachverhalt: A regional court awards C the right to the grant of the European patent on D's application EP-D for all designated States. The judgment has been final since Monday, 15 June 2026. The grant proceedings before the EPO have been stayed since 2025.

einheit:e01n61-4a.frage: Can C prosecute application EP-D as its own application?
loesung: **Yes.** The entitled person may prosecute the application as its own in place of the applicant (Art. 61(1)(a) EPC). C declares this in writing; the proceedings resume at the stage at which they were stayed (Guidelines A-IV, 2.4). Alternatives: new application (Art. 61(1)(b) EPC) or refusal (Art. 61(1)(c) EPC).
einheit:e01n61-4a.merke: Art. 61(1) EPC: prosecute, file anew or have it refused.

einheit:e01n61-4b.frage: By when must C avail itself of one of the remedies?
loesung: **By 15 September 2026.** The remedies of Art. 61(1) EPC are available only within three months after the decision has become final (R. 16(1)(a) EPC); further processing is excluded (R. 135(2) EPC). Before then, the EPO does not resume the proceedings unless C requests it (R. 14(2) EPC).
einheit:e01n61-4b.merke: Three months from the decision becoming final.

einheit:e01n61-4c.frage: Can C still proceed under Art. 61(1) EPC?
loesung: **No.** The remedies require that the European patent has not yet been granted (R. 16(1)(b) EPC). C is left with national law: transfer of the patent, or revocation because D was not entitled (Art. 138(1)(e) EPC).
einheit:e01n61-4c.merke: After grant, Art. 61 EPC no longer helps.
einheit:e01n61-4c.abwandlung: C had not obtained a stay; EP-D was granted before the judgment became final.

gruppe:e01n61-5.sachverhalt: In 2024, E files application EP-E for an invention actually made by F. At the end of 2025, E withdraws the application before F sues. Later, a court awards F, by final decision, the right to the grant of a European patent for this invention.

einheit:e01n61-5a.frage: Can F file a new application under Art. 61(1)(b) EPC although EP-E is no longer pending?
loesung: **Yes.** It is not a requirement that the original application still be pending when the new application is filed (G 3/92). However, F must observe the three months after the decision has become final (R. 16(1)(a) EPC).
einheit:e01n61-5a.merke: A new application under Art. 61 EPC does not need a pending original application.

einheit:e01n61-5b.frage: Does the new application obtain the date of filing of EP-E?
loesung: **Yes,** insofar as it does not extend beyond the content of EP-E as filed: Art. 76(1) EPC applies mutatis mutandis (Art. 61(2) EPC). F files it directly with the EPO and pays the filing and search fees within one month (R. 17(2) EPC).
einheit:e01n61-5b.merke: The new application is treated like a divisional application.

einheit:e01n61-5c.frage: Must F pay renewal fees for past years for the new application?
loesung: **No.** No renewal fees are payable for the year in which the new application is filed or for the preceding years (R. 51(6) EPC). In this respect it differs from a divisional application (R. 51(3) EPC).
einheit:e01n61-5c.merke: No back renewal fees for a new application under Art. 61 EPC.

kapitel:e01n65.titel: Art. 64 and 65 EPC: validation and unitary patent

einheit:e01n65-0.titel: After grant: bundle or unitary patent
einheit:e01n65-0.text: From the mention of grant, the European patent has the effect of a national patent in each designated State (Art. 64(1) EPC). What else is needed is determined by each State: a translation under Art. 65 EPC, unless it has dispensed with it under the London Agreement, and renewal fees to the national office (Art. 141 EPC). For the participating EU States there is instead the **unitary patent**: request within **one month** of the mention of grant (R. 6(1) UPR). Paper D 2024 tested exactly this combination: United Kingdom, Poland and unitary patent for an applicant from Morocco.

gruppe:e01n65-1.sachverhalt: H's European patent EP-H protects a process for manufacturing substance S. The decision to grant is dated 6 August 2026; the mention of grant is published on 2 September 2026. W manufactures S in France using the process and sells S in Germany.

einheit:e01n65-1a.frage: From when does EP-H confer the rights under the patent?
optionen: From expiry of the opposition period
loesung: **From 2 September 2026.** The patent confers its rights from the date of publication of the mention of grant (Art. 64(1) EPC); the decision to grant also takes effect on that date (Art. 97(3) EPC). Before then, only the provisional protection of the published application exists (Art. 67 EPC).
einheit:e01n65-1a.merke: What counts is the mention of grant in the Bulletin.
einheit:e01n65-1a.abschnitt: Art. 64 EPC: effect of the patent

einheit:e01n65-1b.frage: Can H take action against the sale of S in Germany although the process is not used there?
loesung: **Yes.** If the subject-matter of the patent is a process, the protection extends to the products directly obtained by that process (Art. 64(2) EPC). The sale of S affects the German part of EP-H.
einheit:e01n65-1b.merke: Process protection covers the direct product.
einheit:e01n65-1b.abschnitt: Art. 64 EPC: effect of the patent

einheit:e01n65-1c.frage: Is the question whether W infringes the patent governed by the EPC?
loesung: **No.** Any infringement of a European patent is dealt with by national law (Art. 64(3) EPC). The EPC only lays down that the extent of protection is determined by the claims (Art. 69 EPC).
einheit:e01n65-1c.merke: Infringement: national law; extent of protection: Art. 69 EPC.
einheit:e01n65-1c.abschnitt: Art. 64 EPC: effect of the patent

gruppe:e01n65-2.titel: From the United Kingdom to Morocco
gruppe:e01n65-2.sachverhalt: J S.A., based in Morocco, obtains European patent EP-J in French; the mention of grant is published on Wednesday, 2 September 2026. J wants protection in the United Kingdom, Poland and Morocco. J never paid a validation fee for Morocco.

einheit:e01n65-2a.frage: Must J file a translation for the United Kingdom?
loesung: **No.** As a party to the London Agreement, the United Kingdom has dispensed with translations under Art. 65(1) EPC; its official language, English, is an official language of the EPO. The patent takes effect there without further action (Art. 64(1) EPC).
einheit:e01n65-2a.merke: London Agreement States with an EPO official language require no translation.

einheit:e01n65-2b.frage: By when must J file the Polish translation if Poland provides for no longer period?
loesung: **By 2 December 2026.** Poland is not a party to the London Agreement and requires a translation (Art. 65(1) EPC). The period ends three months after the mention of grant. If J misses it, Poland may treat the effects as void ab initio (Art. 65(3) EPC).
einheit:e01n65-2b.merke: Art. 65 EPC: three months from the mention of grant.

einheit:e01n65-2c.frage: Can J still obtain protection in Morocco now by paying the validation fee?
loesung: **No.** The validation fee had to be paid within six months of the mention of publication of the search report, or with a surcharge within a further two months (Guidelines A-III, 12.2). There is no re-establishment of rights; validation is governed by national law, not by the EPC (Guidelines A-III, 12.1).
einheit:e01n65-2c.merke: Validation States: fee during the application phase, no re-establishment.

gruppe:e01n65-3.sachverhalt: For K's European patent EP-K, the mention of grant is published on Wednesday, 7 October 2026. The language of the proceedings is German; the claims are the same for all States. K wants a unitary patent and, in addition, protection in Spain.

einheit:e01n65-3a.frage: By when must K file the request for unitary effect?
loesung: **By 9 November 2026.** The request must be filed with the EPO no later than one month after publication of the mention of grant (R. 6(1) UPR). The period would end on Saturday, 7 November 2026, and is extended to Monday (R. 134(1) EPC, applicable mutatis mutandis under R. 20(2) UPR).
einheit:e01n65-3a.merke: Unitary effect: one month from the mention of grant.

einheit:e01n65-3b.frage: Is a request in German without a translation of the patent specification sufficient?
loesung: **No.** The request must be filed in writing in the language of the proceedings, here German. During the transitional period it must include a full translation of the specification into English (R. 6(2) UPR, Art. 6(1) TranslReg). If it is missing, the EPO invites K to remedy this within one month (R. 7(3) UPR).
einheit:e01n65-3b.merke: Request in the language of the proceedings, translation into or from English.

einheit:e01n65-3c.frage: K misses the one-month time limit. Can K request further processing?
loesung: **No.** Art. 121 EPC is not among the provisions that R. 20(1) UPR declares applicable mutatis mutandis. Only re-establishment of rights is possible, to be requested within two months of expiry of the missed time limit (R. 22(2) UPR).
einheit:e01n65-3c.merke: Request deadline missed: re-establishment within two months, no further processing.

einheit:e01n65-3d.frage: Does the unitary patent also extend to Spain?
loesung: **No.** Unitary effect exists only in the participating Member States in which the Unified Patent Court has exclusive jurisdiction on the date of registration (Art. 18(2) UPReg). Spain does not participate; there K must validate the European patent under Art. 65 EPC and national law.
einheit:e01n65-3d.merke: Unitary patent and national validation can be combined.

gruppe:e01n65-4.sachverhalt: L's application was filed on 15 November 2021. The mention of grant is published on 7 October 2026. L validates the patent in Poland and has unitary effect registered for the participating States.

einheit:e01n65-4a.titel: Last renewal fee to the EPO
einheit:e01n65-4a.frage: Does L pay the renewal fee for the fifth year, due on 30 November 2025, to the EPO?
loesung: **Yes.** The obligation to pay renewal fees to the EPO ends with the fee for the year in which the mention of grant is published (Art. 86(2) EPC). 7 October 2026 falls in the fifth year (15 November 2025 to 14 November 2026).
einheit:e01n65-4a.merke: To the EPO: up to and including the year of the mention of grant.
einheit:e01n65-4a.abschnitt: Art. 86(2) EPC, Art. 141 EPC: renewal fees

einheit:e01n65-4b.frage: Must L pay an additional fee for Poland if he pays the sixth-year fee, due on 30 November 2026, on 4 December 2026?
loesung: **No.** National renewal fees falling due within two months of the mention of grant are deemed validly paid if paid within that period, here by 7 December 2026; no additional fee is charged (Art. 141(2) EPC).
einheit:e01n65-4b.merke: Art. 141(2) EPC: two months' grace after grant.
einheit:e01n65-4b.abschnitt: Art. 86(2) EPC, Art. 141 EPC: renewal fees

einheit:e01n65-4c.titel: Renewal fees for the unitary patent
einheit:e01n65-4c.frage: Does L pay the renewal fees for the unitary patent to the national offices?
loesung: **No.** Renewal fees for the unitary patent are paid to the EPO, once for all participating States (R. 13(1) UPR). A fee that would have fallen due between the mention of grant and the communication of registration falls due only with that communication and may be paid within three months without an additional fee (R. 13(5) UPR).
einheit:e01n65-4c.merke: Unitary patent: renewal fees to the EPO.
einheit:e01n65-4c.abschnitt: Art. 86(2) EPC, Art. 141 EPC: renewal fees

kapitel:e01n76.titel: Art. 76 EPC, R. 36 EPC: divisional application

einheit:e01n76-0.titel: As long as the parent is alive
einheit:e01n76-0.text: In Paper D, the divisional application is the all-purpose tool: for a second invention (2021), for unsearched subject-matter (2023), for an additional claim after remittal (2025) or after resumption of stayed proceedings (2019). Four checkpoints: Is the parent application **pending** (R. 36(1) EPC, G 1/09)? Is the **language** right (R. 36(2) EPC)? Does the **content** not extend beyond the parent application (Art. 76(1) EPC)? Have the **fees** been paid, including back renewal fees (R. 36(3) EPC, R. 51(3) EPC)?

gruppe:e01n76-1.sachverhalt: S has three European applications. For EP-1, the mention of grant is published on Wednesday, 7 October 2026. EP-2 was refused by decision of 9 September 2026; S does not appeal. For EP-3, the renewal fee due on 30 April 2026 is unpaid; the grace period with additional fee is still running.

einheit:e01n76-1a.frage: Can S still file a divisional application on EP-1 on 7 October 2026?
loesung: **No.** The application is pending up to the day before the mention of grant, not on that day (Guidelines A-IV, 1.1.1); R. 134 EPC does not extend this. The last opportunity was 6 October 2026.
einheit:e01n76-1a.merke: Mention of grant: divisional application at the latest the day before.

einheit:e01n76-1b.frage: Can S still file a divisional application on EP-2 on 5 November 2026?
loesung: **Yes.** A refused application remains pending without an appeal until the period for appeal expires (G 1/09). The period is two months after notification (Art. 108 EPC); the decision is deemed notified on 9 September 2026 (R. 126(2) and 127(2) EPC), so the period ends on 9 November 2026.
einheit:e01n76-1b.merke: Refusal: pending until the end of the period for appeal.

einheit:e01n76-1c.frage: Can S now file a divisional application on EP-3 although S no longer intends to pay the renewal fee?
loesung: **Yes.** If a renewal fee is not paid on the due date, the application remains pending until the end of the grace period under R. 51(2) EPC, even if the fee is ultimately not paid (Guidelines A-IV, 1.1.1). Only on expiry of the grace period is it deemed to be withdrawn (Art. 86(1) EPC).
einheit:e01n76-1c.merke: During the grace period the application remains pending.

gruppe:e01n76-2.sachverhalt: T's English-language application EP-T, filed on 10 April 2023, describes inventions X and Y; only X has been searched and claimed. T does not reply to a communication of 2 June 2026 setting a four-month period. On 25 September 2026, T files a divisional application for Y in French.

loesung: **No.** A divisional application on an application in an official language must be filed in the language of the proceedings of the parent, here English (R. 36(2) EPC). A subsequently filed translation or a correction under R. 139 EPC does not cure this (J 13/14). EP-T was still pending on 25 September 2026.
einheit:e01n76-2a.merke: Divisional application: in the language of the proceedings of the parent application.
einheit:e01n76-2a.abschnitt: R. 36(2) and 36(3) EPC: language and fees

einheit:e01n76-2b.frage: The period for reply expired on 2 October 2026. Is a divisional application filed in English on 27 October 2026 valid if T does not remedy the loss of rights?
loesung: **No.** On expiry of the period, EP-T is deemed to be withdrawn (Art. 94(4) EPC) and is no longer pending. The divisional application only becomes valid if T requests further processing: pay the fee and reply to the communication (Art. 121 EPC, R. 135(1) EPC). EP-T is then deemed pending throughout (Guidelines A-IV, 1.1.1).
einheit:e01n76-2b.merke: No valid divisional application without remedying the loss of rights.
einheit:e01n76-2b.abschnitt: R. 36(2) and 36(3) EPC: language and fees

einheit:e01n76-2c.frage: Must T also pay renewal fees for the new divisional application?
loesung: **Yes.** The renewal fees for the third and fourth years already due for EP-T (due on 30 April 2025 and 30 April 2026) must also be paid for the divisional. They fall due on its filing and may be paid within four months without an additional fee (R. 51(3) EPC). Filing and search fees: within one month (R. 36(3) EPC).
einheit:e01n76-2c.merke: Back renewal fees: four months from filing the divisional application.
einheit:e01n76-2c.abschnitt: R. 36(2) and 36(3) EPC: language and fees

gruppe:e01n76-3.sachverhalt: Parent application EP-1 describes a pump with features A and B, B being presented as essential, and an embodiment with the addition C. Divisional application EP-2 takes over the description without the embodiment with C and claims A alone. EP-1 has since been granted.

einheit:e01n76-3a.frage: Is EP-2 lost because it extends beyond EP-1 and EP-1 is no longer pending?
loesung: **No.** A divisional application which, as filed, extends beyond the parent application can still be amended to comply with Art. 76(1) EPC, even if the parent is no longer pending (G 1/05). If the claim is limited to A and B, EP-2 obtains the date of filing and priority of EP-1.
einheit:e01n76-3a.merke: Added matter in a divisional application can be cured.

einheit:e01n76-3b.frage: Divisional application EP-3, claiming A, B and C, is divided out of EP-2. Is that allowable?
loesung: **No.** In a chain, the content of each divisional application must be derivable from each preceding application as filed (G 1/06). C is missing from EP-2; the fact that EP-1 discloses it is not enough.

einheit:e01n76-3c.frage: Does it matter for filing EP-3 whether EP-1 is still pending?
loesung: **No.** For a divisional of a divisional application, it suffices that the immediately preceding application, here EP-2, is pending (Guidelines A-IV, 1.1.1). For EP-3, as a second-generation divisional, an additional fee is payable as part of the filing fee (R. 38(4) EPC).
einheit:e01n76-3c.merke: What counts is the direct predecessor.

gruppe:e01n76-4.sachverhalt: U's application EP-U describes a valve with features E and F and an unrelated valve G. Only G has been searched and claimed. Grant is imminent; U also wants to protect E and F and to obtain a further dependent claim for G.

einheit:e01n76-4a.frage: Can U switch the claims of EP-U to E and F?
loesung: **No.** Amended claims may not relate to unsearched subject-matter which does not combine with the originally claimed invention to form a single general inventive concept (R. 137(5) EPC). The way forward is a divisional application while EP-U is pending; a separate search fee is payable for it within one month (R. 36(3) EPC).
einheit:e01n76-4a.abschnitt: Art. 76(1) and 76(2) EPC: the divisional application as a tool

einheit:e01n76-4b.frage: When is the designation fee for the divisional application payable?
optionen: Within six months of the mention of publication of the search report on the divisional application
Not at all, it is covered by the fee paid for EP-U
loesung: **Within six months of the mention of publication of the search report on the divisional application** (R. 36(4) EPC). Designated are the States designated in EP-U when the divisional application is filed (Art. 76(2) EPC). If the time limit is missed, further processing is available (Guidelines A-IV, 1.4.1).
einheit:e01n76-4b.merke: Designation fee for the divisional: linked to its own search report.
einheit:e01n76-4b.abschnitt: Art. 76(1) and 76(2) EPC: the divisional application as a tool

einheit:e01n76-4c.frage: U files a second divisional application with the same claims to G plus the additional dependent claim. Can it lead to a patent alongside EP-U?
loesung: **No.** An application can be refused if it claims the same subject-matter as a European patent granted to the same applicant, also as between parent and divisional application (G 4/19). U should withdraw EP-U after filing the divisional application but before the mention of grant.
einheit:e01n76-4c.merke: The same claims can only be granted once.
einheit:e01n76-4c.abschnitt: Art. 76(1) and 76(2) EPC: the divisional application as a tool

kapitel:e01n80.titel: Art. 80 EPC, R. 40, 56, 56a and 58 EPC: date of filing and missing parts

einheit:e01n80-0.titel: What a date of filing requires
einheit:e01n80-0.text: Three things suffice for a date of filing: an indication that a European patent is sought, information concerning the applicant, and a description or a reference to a previously filed application (Art. 80 EPC, R. 40(1) EPC). Claims, fees and an official language are not needed. Paper D mainly tests what happens next: missing parts or drawings (R. 56 EPC, 2015 and 2018), erroneously filed documents (R. 56a EPC, 2025), missing claims (R. 58 EPC, 2019) and filing by reference (2017). Re-dating can blow the priority period; that is why saving the date via the priority and withdrawal matter.

gruppe:e01n80-1.sachverhalt: Today, the last day of the priority year, representative V is to file a European application for a Japanese colleague, claiming priority from Japanese application JP 4711. The attachments containing the application text and the applicant's details cannot be opened; the colleague cannot be reached today.

einheit:e01n80-1a.frage: Can V obtain a date of filing without the applicant's name?
loesung: **Yes.** R. 40(1)(b) EPC requires information allowing the identity of the applicant to be established **or** allowing the applicant to be contacted. The representative's name and address suffice (Guidelines A-II, 4.1.2).
einheit:e01n80-1a.merke: Contact details suffice for a date of filing.
einheit:e01n80-1a.abschnitt: R. 40 EPC: requirements for a date of filing

einheit:e01n80-1b.frage: How does V replace the missing description?
optionen: Not at all; without a description there is no date of filing
By a reference to JP 4711 stating its date of filing, number and office, and that it replaces the description and drawings
By claims that V drafts from memory
By requesting an extension of time
loesung: **By a reference to JP 4711.** Instead of a description, a reference to a previously filed application suffices (R. 40(1)(c) EPC). It must state the date of filing, number and office and indicate that it replaces the description and drawings (R. 40(2) EPC).
einheit:e01n80-1b.merke: Reference: date, number, office, replacement statement.
einheit:e01n80-1b.abschnitt: R. 40 EPC: requirements for a date of filing

einheit:e01n80-1c.frage: Is the date of filing lost if V does not file the certified copy of JP 4711 within two months?
loesung: **No.** The copy and translation must be filed within two months (R. 40(3) EPC). If the copy is missing, the EPO issues an invitation under R. 55 EPC; if it is received within two months of that communication, the original date of filing is kept (Guidelines A-II, 4.1.5). One copy also serves for the priority.
einheit:e01n80-1c.merke: Reference: copy within two months, if need be after an invitation.
einheit:e01n80-1c.abschnitt: R. 40 EPC: requirements for a date of filing

gruppe:e01n80-2.titel: Claims and drawings, but no description
gruppe:e01n80-2.sachverhalt: Z, an inventor resident in Argentina, files a European application online in Spanish on Monday, 2 February 2026, without claiming priority. It contains only claims and drawings. Z files the description on 16 February 2026.

einheit:e01n80-2a.frage: Is 2 February 2026 the date of filing?
loesung: **No.** Without a description or a reference, R. 40(1)(c) EPC is not met. The date of filing is the date on which all requirements are fulfilled, here 16 February 2026 (Guidelines A-II, 4.1.5). R. 56 EPC does not apply: not parts of the description were missing, but the whole of it.
einheit:e01n80-2a.merke: No description: date of filing only once it is filed.

einheit:e01n80-2b.frage: Did Z have to appoint a professional representative just to file the application?
loesung: **No.** A person having neither residence nor principal place of business in a Contracting State must be represented, except for filing the application (Art. 133(2) EPC). For all further acts, Z needs a professional representative.

gruppe:e01n80-3.sachverhalt: On Friday, 13 March 2026, the last day of the priority year, W files EP-W1 claiming priority from GB-1 and EP-W2 claiming priority from GB-2. EP-W1 lacks the drawings referred to in the description; GB-1 contains them identically. On 20 March 2026 W files them, and for EP-W2 also newly drawn figures not contained in GB-2.

einheit:e01n80-3a.frage: Can EP-W1 keep the date of filing 13 March 2026?
loesung: **Yes.** The drawings are completely contained in GB-1, whose priority was claimed on the date of filing. By 13 May 2026, W must request that they be based on the priority, file a copy (unless available under R. 53(2) EPC) and indicate where they appear in GB-1 (R. 56(3) EPC).
einheit:e01n80-3a.merke: Contained in the priority application: the date of filing stays.
einheit:e01n80-3a.abschnitt: R. 56 EPC: missing parts and drawings

einheit:e01n80-3b.frage: Does EP-W2 keep the priority of GB-2?
loesung: **No.** The figures are not contained in GB-2; the application is re-dated to 20 March 2026 (R. 56(2) EPC). That date lies after expiry of the twelve months (Art. 87(1) EPC); the priority claim is invalid.
einheit:e01n80-3b.abschnitt: R. 56 EPC: missing parts and drawings

einheit:e01n80-3c.frage: Can W recover the date of filing 13 March 2026 for EP-W2?
loesung: **Yes,** by withdrawing the later-filed figures within one month of the notification of the re-dating (R. 56(6) EPC). The re-dating is then deemed not to have been made, and references to the figures are deemed deleted (R. 56(4) EPC). The figures are then not part of the application.
einheit:e01n80-3c.merke: Withdrawal: old date, but without the parts.
einheit:e01n80-3c.abschnitt: R. 56 EPC: missing parts and drawings

einheit:e01n80-3d.frage: Can W request further processing if he misses the one-month period?
loesung: **No.** The time limits under R. 56 EPC are excluded from further processing (R. 135(2) EPC). Only re-establishment of rights is possible (Art. 122 EPC).
einheit:e01n80-3d.abschnitt: R. 56 EPC: missing parts and drawings

gruppe:e01n80-4.sachverhalt: On Thursday, 15 January 2026, Y files EP-Y1 claiming priority from Italian application IT-Y concerning invention A. By mistake, she uploads the description and claims of another application concerning invention B. A was published in a journal during the priority interval. On 2 March 2026 Y notices the error.

einheit:e01n80-4a.frage: By when must Y file the correct documents to keep the date of filing?
loesung: **By 16 March 2026.** The period is two months from the date of filing (R. 56a(3) EPC) and ends on Sunday, 15 March 2026, extended to Monday (R. 134(1) EPC). Within the same period Y must request that the documents be based on IT-Y, file a copy and translation and indicate where they are contained (R. 56a(4) EPC).
einheit:e01n80-4a.merke: Erroneously filed: two months, rescue via the priority.
einheit:e01n80-4a.abschnitt: R. 56a EPC: erroneously filed application documents

einheit:e01n80-4b.frage: Do the documents concerning B then disappear from EP-Y1?
loesung: **No.** If the date of filing is kept under R. 56a(4) EPC, the correct documents are included and the erroneous ones remain in the application. They can only be removed by amendment within the limits of Art. 123(2) EPC (Guidelines A-II, 6.4). Once published, they may be a prior right against a later application concerning B (Art. 54(3) EPC).
einheit:e01n80-4b.merke: The priority saves the date, but the wrong documents remain.
einheit:e01n80-4b.abschnitt: R. 56a EPC: erroneously filed application documents

einheit:e01n80-4c.frage: Does the date of filing remain 15 January 2026 if Y files the correct documents on 2 March 2026?
loesung: **No.** Without a priority claim on the date of filing there is no rescue under R. 56a(4) EPC (Guidelines A-II, 6.4.1). The application is re-dated to 2 March 2026, and the erroneous documents are deemed not to have been filed (R. 56a(3) EPC).
einheit:e01n80-4c.merke: No priority claim on the date of filing: re-dating.
einheit:e01n80-4c.abwandlung: EP-Y1 claimed no priority when filed.
einheit:e01n80-4c.abschnitt: R. 56a EPC: erroneously filed application documents

gruppe:e01n80-5.sachverhalt: On the last day of the priority year, X files EP-X claiming priority from German application DE-1. The description matches DE-1 and describes only aluminium capsules; the claims of DE-1 cover aluminium capsules and metal capsules. X forgets the claims. During the priority interval an article on both was published.

einheit:e01n80-5a.frage: Is EP-X accorded a date of filing?
loesung: **Yes.** Claims are not a requirement for a date of filing (R. 40(1) EPC). X can file them of his own motion or within two months of the EPO's invitation (R. 57 and 58 EPC; Guidelines A-III, 15).
einheit:e01n80-5a.merke: No claims, but still a date of filing.

einheit:e01n80-5b.frage: May X file a later claim to metal capsules?
loesung: **No.** Later-filed claims need a basis in the description and drawings as at the date of filing (Art. 123(2) EPC); the description only discloses aluminium, and the claims of DE-1 do not count. A claim to aluminium capsules enjoys the priority; the article is not state of the art for it.
einheit:e01n80-5b.merke: Later-filed claims: basis only in the description as filed.

einheit:e01n80-5c.frage: X files no claims even after the invitation. Can X request further processing?
loesung: **No.** The application is refused (Art. 90(5) EPC). The time limit under R. 58 EPC is excluded from further processing (R. 135(2) EPC); re-establishment of rights or an appeal remain possible (Guidelines A-III, 15).
einheit:e01n80-5c.merke: No claims: refusal, no further processing.

kapitel:e01n86.titel: Art. 86 EPC, R. 51 EPC: renewal fees

einheit:e01n86-0.titel: Due date, grace period, loss of rights
einheit:e01n86-0.text: Renewal fees appear in Paper D almost every time as a side issue: in 2022 after re-establishment of rights (Question 1) and shortly before grant (Question 2), in 2025 with the automatic debiting procedure (Question 4). The framework: fees from the **third year**, due on the **last day of the month** containing the anniversary of the date of filing (R. 51(1) EPC); a six-month grace period with an additional fee (R. 51(2) EPC), and only then is the application deemed to be withdrawn (Art. 86(1) EPC). No further processing, only re-establishment of rights. Special rules apply to divisional applications (R. 51(3) EPC) and after re-establishment (R. 51(4) EPC); after grant the states collect the fees (Art. 141 EPC), for the Unitary Patent the EPO.

gruppe:e01n86-1.sachverhalt: A files a European patent application on 14 March 2024. Her accounts department wants to pay all renewal fees as early as possible and transfers the renewal fee for the third year on 15 September 2025.

einheit:e01n86-1a.frage: When does the renewal fee for the third year fall due?
loesung: **On 31 March 2026.** Renewal fees for the coming year are due on the last day of the month containing the anniversary of the date of filing (first sentence of R. 51(1) EPC). The third year begins on 14 March 2026; the fee falls due at the end of the month (Art. 86(1) EPC).
einheit:e01n86-1a.merke: Due on the last day of the anniversary month.
einheit:e01n86-1a.abschnitt: R. 51(1) EPC: due date and advance payment

einheit:e01n86-1b.frage: Is the payment of 15 September 2025 valid?
loesung: **No.** The fee for the third year may be validly paid at the earliest six months before it falls due (second sentence of R. 51(1) EPC), i.e. from 30 September 2025. An earlier payment is not valid; the EPO refunds it (Guidelines A-X, 5.2.4).
einheit:e01n86-1b.merke: Third year: at most six months in advance.
einheit:e01n86-1b.abschnitt: R. 51(1) EPC: due date and advance payment

einheit:e01n86-1c.frage: Can A pay the renewal fee for the fourth year as early as October 2026?
loesung: **No.** All renewal fees other than the third may be validly paid at the earliest three months before they fall due (third sentence of R. 51(1) EPC). The fourth fee falls due on 31 March 2027.
einheit:e01n86-1c.merke: From the fourth year: at most three months in advance.
einheit:e01n86-1c.abschnitt: R. 51(1) EPC: due date and advance payment

gruppe:e01n86-2.sachverhalt: B files a European patent application on 12 September 2023. The renewal fee for the third year falls due on 30 September 2025; B does not pay it.

einheit:e01n86-2a.frage: Until when can B still pay the fee with the additional fee?
loesung: **Until 31 March 2026.** The grace period is six months from the due date (first sentence of R. 51(2) EPC). It runs from the last day of a month to the last day of a month, i.e. it ends on the last day of the sixth month (J 4/91; Guidelines A-X, 5.2.4).
einheit:e01n86-2a.merke: Grace period: from month end to month end.
einheit:e01n86-2a.abschnitt: R. 51(2) EPC: grace period and loss of rights

einheit:e01n86-2b.titel: Time of the loss of rights
einheit:e01n86-2b.frage: Is the application already deemed to be withdrawn on 1 October 2025?
loesung: **No.** The deemed withdrawal under Art. 86(1) EPC only takes effect on expiry of the six-month period (second sentence of R. 51(2) EPC).
einheit:e01n86-2b.merke: Loss of rights only once the grace period has expired.
einheit:e01n86-2b.abschnitt: R. 51(2) EPC: grace period and loss of rights

einheit:e01n86-2c.frage: Can B still file a divisional application on 16 March 2026?
loesung: **Yes.** Until the grace period expires the application is pending; a divisional application may be filed relating to any pending earlier application (R. 36(1) EPC).
einheit:e01n86-2c.merke: During the grace period the application is still pending.
einheit:e01n86-2c.abschnitt: R. 51(2) EPC: grace period and loss of rights

einheit:e01n86-2d.frage: B does not pay by 31 March 2026 either. Is re-establishment of rights B's only option?
loesung: **Yes.** Further processing is excluded for R. 51(2) EPC (R. 135(2) EPC). Re-establishment requires all due care (Art. 122(1) EPC). The request must be filed at the latest one year after expiry of the grace period (R. 136(1) EPC).
einheit:e01n86-2d.abschnitt: R. 51(2) EPC: grace period and loss of rights

gruppe:e01n86-3.sachverhalt: C's parent application was filed on 15 April 2021; all renewal fees have been paid. On 3 March 2026 C files a divisional application.

einheit:e01n86-3a.frage: Which renewal fees for the divisional application fall due on its filing?
optionen: None, the divisional starts with the first year
Only the fee for the fifth year
The fees for the third to fifth years
The fees for the third to sixth years
loesung: **The fees for the third to fifth years.** Fees already due for the parent application up to the filing must also be paid for the divisional and fall due on its filing (first sentence of R. 51(3) EPC). The years are counted from the date of filing of the parent application (Art. 76(1) EPC).
einheit:e01n86-3a.merke: The divisional inherits the age of the parent.

einheit:e01n86-3b.frage: Can C still pay the sixth-year fee, due on 30 April 2026, on 3 July 2026 without an additional fee?
loesung: **Yes.** A renewal fee falling due within four months of filing the divisional may, like the back-payable fees, be paid within that period without an additional fee (second sentence of R. 51(3) EPC). The period ends on 3 July 2026.
einheit:e01n86-3b.merke: Four months without an additional fee – also for the fee newly falling due.

einheit:e01n86-3c.frage: Until when can C pay the fifth-year fee with the additional fee if he misses the four months?
loesung: **Until 3 September 2026.** R. 51(2) EPC applies (third sentence of R. 51(3) EPC): six months from the due date, and the fee fell due on the date of filing (Guidelines A-IV, 1.4.3).
einheit:e01n86-3c.merke: Grace period runs from filing of the divisional.

gruppe:e01n86-4.sachverhalt: D's application (date of filing 18 March 2021) is deemed to be withdrawn because the time limit for replying to a communication expired on 15 January 2026. D is granted re-establishment of rights in the time limit for further processing; the decision is notified on 9 October 2026. The sixth-year fee is unpaid.

einheit:e01n86-4a.frage: Did D have to pay the fee due on 31 March 2026 with the additional fee by 30 September 2026 to save the application?
loesung: **No.** A renewal fee that would have fallen due between the loss of rights (15 January 2026) and the notification of the decision on re-establishment only falls due on the date of that notification (R. 51(4)(a) EPC).
einheit:e01n86-4a.merke: No renewal fee falls due while rights are lost.

einheit:e01n86-4b.frage: Until when can D pay the fee without an additional fee?
loesung: **Until 9 February 2027.** The postponed fee may be paid within four months of notification of the decision without an additional fee (R. 51(4)(a) EPC); thereafter the six-month grace period with an additional fee applies (R. 51(2) EPC).
einheit:e01n86-4b.merke: After re-establishment: four months without an additional fee.

einheit:e01n86-4c.frage: Can D validly pay a fee that fell due on 31 October 2025 and is still unpaid after 30 April 2026?
loesung: **Yes.** If the fee was already due at the loss of rights but the grace period had not yet expired, it may be paid within six months of notification of the decision on re-establishment, together with the additional fee (R. 51(4)(b) EPC).
einheit:e01n86-4c.merke: Running grace period: six months from notification, with additional fee.
einheit:e01n86-4c.abwandlung: The date of filing was 20 October 2020; the sixth-year fee fell due on 31 October 2025.

gruppe:e01n86-5.sachverhalt: E's application was filed on 12 May 2021. The mention of the grant is published in the European Patent Bulletin on 6 May 2026. The sixth-year fee would fall due on 31 May 2026.

einheit:e01n86-5a.titel: Last fee payable to the EPO
einheit:e01n86-5a.frage: Must E pay the sixth-year fee to the EPO?
loesung: **No.** The obligation to pay the EPO ends with the fee for the year in which the mention of the grant is published (Art. 86(2) EPC). The fifth year runs until 11 May 2026; from the sixth year, the Contracting States levy the fees (Art. 141(1) EPC).
einheit:e01n86-5a.merke: What counts is the patent year of the mention of grant.

einheit:e01n86-5b.frage: Can E still pay the national sixth-year fee on 3 July 2026 without an additional fee?
loesung: **Yes.** A renewal fee falling due within two months of publication of the mention of the grant is deemed validly paid if paid within that period; no national additional fee is charged (Art. 141(2) EPC). The period ends on 6 July 2026.

einheit:e01n86-5c.frage: To whom does E pay the renewal fees if E obtains unitary effect for the patent?
loesung: **To the EPO.** For patents with unitary effect, renewal fees and additional fees are payable to the European Patent Organisation, i.e. to the EPO (Art. 11(1) UPReg, R. 13(1) UPR).
einheit:e01n86-5c.merke: Unitary Patent: one renewal fee to the EPO.

kapitel:e01n87.titel: Art. 87 to 89 EPC, R. 52 and 53 EPC: priority

einheit:e01n87-0.titel: No valid priority, no priority date
einheit:e01n87-0.text: Hardly any Paper D does without priority: it determines which document is state of the art (Art. 89 EPC). Tested are the **first application** (2019 Question 4, Art. 87(4) EPC), the **same invention** (2017 Question 4, G 2/98), **partial priority** (2021 Question 4, 2022 Question 5, G 1/15), the validity of the priority document (2022 Question 4), declaration, copy and translation (R. 52 and 53 EPC; 2015 Question 2, 2025 Question 2) and withdrawing a priority to postpone time limits (2025 Question 1). The priority period itself can only be saved by re-establishment of rights; entitlement is presumed under G 1/22.

gruppe:e01n87-1.sachverhalt: On 5 February 2024 E files a Canadian application CA for device V; it is published on 6 August 2025. On 4 November 2024 E files device V in Korea (KR). On 3 November 2025 E files a European application for V claiming the priority of KR.

einheit:e01n87-1a.frage: Is KR a first application within the meaning of Art. 87(1) EPC?
loesung: **No.** E had already filed V with CA. Art. 87(4) EPC does not help: CA was filed in a different state, was not withdrawn and was later published. The priority is invalid, even without examining the content of KR (Guidelines F-VI, 1.4).
einheit:e01n87-1a.merke: Priority only from the same applicant's first application.

einheit:e01n87-1b.frage: Is CA state of the art for the European application?
loesung: **Yes,** under Art. 54(2) EPC: without valid priority the date of filing 3 November 2025 is decisive (Art. 89 EPC does not apply), and CA had been available to the public since 6 August 2025. The claim to V is not new.
einheit:e01n87-1b.merke: Invalid priority: your own earlier application becomes state of the art.

einheit:e01n87-1c.frage: Is KR then a first application?
loesung: **Yes.** A subsequent application in the same state is considered the first application if, by its filing, the earlier one was withdrawn without being published, without leaving rights outstanding and without having served as a basis for claiming priority (Art. 87(4) EPC).
einheit:e01n87-1c.merke: Art. 87(4) EPC: same state, withdrawn without trace.
einheit:e01n87-1c.abwandlung: Instead of CA, E had filed KR0 in Korea on 5 February 2024 and withdrawn it before filing KR, unpublished, without rights outstanding and without priority having been claimed from it.

gruppe:e01n87-2.sachverhalt: On 8 April 2025 F files a US application disclosing a steel screw. On 10 October 2025 a technical article on an aluminium screw is published. On 7 April 2026 F files a European application claiming priority; claim 1 reads "screw made of metal".

einheit:e01n87-2a.frage: Does claim 1 as a whole enjoy the priority of 8 April 2025?
loesung: **No.** The same invention exists only insofar as the skilled person can derive the subject-matter of the claim directly and unambiguously from the previous application as a whole (G 2/98). The US application discloses only steel, not metal in general.
einheit:e01n87-2a.merke: Priority only for what the priority document discloses directly and unambiguously.

einheit:e01n87-2b.frage: Can claim 1 partly enjoy the priority?
loesung: **Yes.** A generic "OR"-claim has partial priority for the alternative disclosed in the priority document for the first time, directly or implicitly, unambiguously and in an enabling manner (G 1/15; Art. 88(3) EPC). For steel, 8 April 2025 applies; for all other metals, 7 April 2026.
einheit:e01n87-2b.merke: Split it conceptually: steel with priority, the rest without.

einheit:e01n87-2c.frage: Does the technical article destroy the novelty of claim 1?
loesung: **Yes.** For the part without priority, the article is state of the art under Art. 54(2) EPC, and aluminium falls within that part. F must limit the claim to steel or to other metals not anticipated.
einheit:e01n87-2c.merke: The intermediate publication hits the part without priority.

einheit:e01n87-2d.frage: Does the technical article then destroy the novelty of claim 1?
loesung: **No.** For the steel part the priority date applies, so the article is not state of the art for it (Art. 89 EPC). The part without priority (other metals) is not anticipated by a steel screw (G 1/15; Guidelines F-VI, 1.5).
einheit:e01n87-2d.merke: Partial priority protects precisely what was published in the interval.
einheit:e01n87-2d.abwandlung: The technical article of 10 October 2025 describes a steel screw.

gruppe:e01n87-3.sachverhalt: On 2 March 2026 G files a European application claiming priority from a Japanese application JP of 3 March 2025. The request mistakenly states 20 February 2025; the EPO points out that the priority lies outside the twelve-month period.

einheit:e01n87-3a.frage: By when can G correct the date?
loesung: **By 2 July 2026.** What counts is whichever 16-month period expires first, from the old (20 June 2026) or the corrected priority date (3 July 2026), but at least four months from the date of filing (R. 52(3) EPC; Guidelines A-III, 6.5.2).
einheit:e01n87-3a.merke: Correction: at least four months from the date of filing.
einheit:e01n87-3a.abschnitt: R. 52 and 53 EPC: declaration, copy, translation

einheit:e01n87-3b.frage: Must G file a translation of JP of his own motion within 16 months?
loesung: **No.** Within 16 months only the copy must be filed, unless it is already available to the EPO (R. 53(1) and 53(2) EPC). The EPO requires a translation only if the validity of the priority is relevant to patentability (R. 53(3) EPC).
einheit:e01n87-3b.merke: Translation of the priority document only on invitation.
einheit:e01n87-3b.abschnitt: R. 52 and 53 EPC: declaration, copy, translation

einheit:e01n87-3c.frage: G lets the time limit for the requested translation expire during examination. Is the priority lost for good?
loesung: **No.** The right of priority is indeed lost (fourth sentence of R. 53(3) EPC). In examination, however, further processing is available, since R. 53 EPC is not listed in R. 135(2) EPC. In opposition the proprietor only has re-establishment of rights (Guidelines A-III, 6.8.3).
