einheit:e01n87-3c.merke: Missed translation: further processing in examination.
einheit:e01n87-3c.abschnitt: R. 52 and 53 EPC: declaration, copy, translation

einheit:e01n87-3d.frage: Can G still save the priority?
loesung: **Yes,** by re-establishment of rights in the priority period: request within two months of its expiry, i.e. by 20 April 2026 (second sentence of R. 136(1) EPC); the European application was filed within that period. G must show all due care (Art. 122(1) EPC; Guidelines A-III, 6.6).
einheit:e01n87-3d.merke: Priority period: re-establishment within two months, subsequent filing within the same period.
einheit:e01n87-3d.abwandlung: JP was in fact filed on 20 February 2025; G missed the priority period through an isolated mistake.
einheit:e01n87-3d.abschnitt: R. 52 and 53 EPC: declaration, copy, translation

gruppe:e01n87-4.sachverhalt: On 8 June 2026 H files a European application claiming two priorities: P1 of 10 June 2025 discloses feature A, P2 of 9 September 2025 feature B. Claim 1 reads "A or B", claim 2 "A and B in combination".

loesung: **Yes.** Multiple priorities may be claimed for any one claim (second sentence of Art. 88(2) EPC). Alternative A is given 10 June 2025, alternative B 9 September 2025 (Guidelines F-VI, 1.5).
einheit:e01n87-4a.merke: Alternatives in one claim can have different priority dates.

einheit:e01n87-4b.frage: Does claim 2 enjoy the priority of P2?
loesung: **No.** Neither priority document discloses the combination of A and B. Priority documents may not be combined in a mosaic; the date of filing 8 June 2026 is decisive (Art. 88(3) EPC; Guidelines F-VI, 1.5).

einheit:e01n87-4c.frage: H withdraws P1 before the technical preparations for publication are completed. When is the application published?
loesung: **After 9 March 2027.** Publication takes place 18 months from the earliest remaining priority date (Art. 93(1)(a) EPC). Time limits running from the priority date are also computed from P2, insofar as they have not yet expired (Guidelines F-VI, 3.5, E-VIII, 1.5).
einheit:e01n87-4c.merke: Withdrawing the earliest priority postpones publication and time limits.

gruppe:e01n87-5.sachverhalt: On 6 November 2024 inventor K alone files a US application. On 5 November 2025 K (for the USA) and L-GmbH (for all other states) jointly file a PCT application claiming the US priority. In European opposition proceedings an opponent disputes L-GmbH's entitlement to priority.

einheit:e01n87-5a.frage: May L-GmbH rely on the priority even though it did not file the US application?
loesung: **Yes.** A party claiming priority under Art. 88(1) EPC is rebuttably presumed to be entitled, even if the priority applicant and the subsequent applicant differ. The joint PCT application establishes an implied agreement allowing L-GmbH to use the priority (G 1/22).
einheit:e01n87-5a.merke: Joint PCT application: agreement to use the priority is presumed.

einheit:e01n87-5b.frage: Who must prove what in the opposition?
optionen: L-GmbH must prove a written assignment before 5 November 2025
Nobody: only national courts have jurisdiction over entitlement
The opponent must rebut the presumption of entitlement
loesung: **The opponent must rebut the presumption.** The EPO is competent to assess entitlement to priority. The presumption is only rebutted by serious factual indications against the agreement (G 1/22).
einheit:e01n87-5b.merke: The burden of proof lies with whoever disputes entitlement.

kapitel:e01n94.titel: Art. 94 and 97 EPC, R. 70 and 71 EPC: examination and grant

einheit:e01n94-0.titel: From the request for examination to the mention of grant
einheit:e01n94-0.text: In Paper D, examination and grant frame many time-limit questions: 2018 (amendment after approval), 2022 (correction in reply to the communication under R. 71(3) EPC), 2023 (unsearched invention) and 2025 (grant after remittal). The sequence: **request for examination** with fee within six months of the mention of the search report (Art. 94(1) EPC, R. 70(1) EPC), together with a reply to a negative search opinion (R. 70a(1) EPC); **communications** under Art. 94(3) EPC; the **communication under R. 71(3) EPC** with four months for fees and translations or for a request for amendment under R. 71(6) EPC; grant takes effect with the mention in the Bulletin (Art. 97(3) EPC).

gruppe:e01n94-1.sachverhalt: In March 2025 A files application EP-A using Form 1001 and pays only the filing and search fees. On 13 May 2026 the European Patent Bulletin mentions the publication of the search report. The search opinion considers claim 1 not new.

einheit:e01n94-1a.titel: Time limit for the request for examination
einheit:e01n94-1a.frage: By when must A request examination?
optionen: Six months from the communication under R. 69 EPC
loesung: **By 13 November 2026.** The period is six months from the mention in the Bulletin (R. 70(1) EPC). Form 1001 already contains the written request, but it is only deemed filed once the examination fee is paid (Art. 94(1) EPC; Guidelines A-VI, 2.2).
einheit:e01n94-1a.merke: Request for examination = form plus fee, six months from the mention of the search report.
einheit:e01n94-1a.abschnitt: Art. 94(1) and 94(2) EPC: request for examination

einheit:e01n94-1b.frage: Must A also reply to the search opinion within the same period?
loesung: **Yes.** If the search opinion is negative, a reply must be filed within the period under R. 70(1) EPC (R. 70a(1) EPC); otherwise the application is deemed to be withdrawn (R. 70a(3) EPC). A mere request for oral proceedings or a general disagreement is not a reply (Guidelines B-XI, 8).
einheit:e01n94-1b.merke: Negative search opinion: a reply is mandatory.
einheit:e01n94-1b.abschnitt: Art. 94(1) and 94(2) EPC: request for examination

einheit:e01n94-1c.frage: By 13 November 2026 A pays neither the examination fee nor the designation fee and does not reply. Is one further processing fee enough?
loesung: **No.** A has omitted three independent acts, each with its own legal consequence (Art. 94(2) EPC, R. 39(2) EPC and R. 70a(3) EPC). A further processing fee must be paid and the act completed for each (R. 135(1) EPC; Guidelines E-VIII, 2).
einheit:e01n94-1c.merke: Independent acts, independent further processing fees.
einheit:e01n94-1c.abschnitt: Art. 94(1) and 94(2) EPC: request for examination

gruppe:e01n94-2.titel: The second invention from the PCT phase
gruppe:e01n94-2.sachverhalt: As International Searching Authority for B's PCT application, the EPO searched only the first of two inventions; B paid no additional search fee. In the European phase there is no supplementary European search. B now directs the claims to the second invention.

einheit:e01n94-2a.frage: Can B still obtain a search for the second invention?
loesung: **Yes.** The Examining Division invites B to pay a search fee for each unsearched invention within two months (R. 164(2)(a) EPC). It sends the results with a communication under Art. 94(3) EPC or with the communication under R. 71(3) EPC (R. 164(2)(b) EPC).
einheit:e01n94-2a.merke: EPO as ISA, invention not searched: fee under R. 164(2) EPC.

einheit:e01n94-2b.frage: B misses the two-month period. Can B request further processing?
loesung: **No.** The time limit under R. 164(2) EPC is excluded from further processing (R. 135(2) EPC) and cannot be extended (Guidelines C-III, 3.1). B must limit the application to a searched invention (R. 164(2) EPC; Guidelines C-III, 3.2.1).

einheit:e01n94-2c.frage: Is the second invention therefore lost for B?
loesung: **No.** B can pursue unsearched subject-matter in a divisional application while the application is pending (Art. 76(1) EPC, R. 36(1) EPC; Guidelines C-III, 3.3). A separate search fee is payable for the divisional (R. 36(3) EPC).
einheit:e01n94-2c.merke: Not searched: divisional instead of examination in the parent.

gruppe:e01n94-3.titel: The communication of the intention to grant
gruppe:e01n94-3.sachverhalt: C filed EP-C in English with 15 claims; during examination these became 17. The communication under R. 71(3) EPC is dated 15 June 2026. C wants a patent as soon as possible but has found an obvious typing error in claim 3.

einheit:e01n94-3a.frage: When does the period for replying to the communication end?
loesung: **On 15 October 2026.** The period is four months (R. 71(3) EPC). The communication is deemed notified on the date it bears (R. 126(2) and 127(2) EPC); the ten days added in older model answers no longer apply.
einheit:e01n94-3a.merke: R. 71(3) EPC: four months from the date of the communication.
einheit:e01n94-3a.abschnitt: R. 71(3) EPC: communication of the intention to grant

einheit:e01n94-3b.frage: Would it suffice to pay the fee for grant and publishing and to translate the claims into German and French?
loesung: **No.** Claims fees are payable for the 16th and 17th claims (R. 71(4) EPC). Only once all fees have been paid and the translations filed is the text deemed approved (R. 71(5) EPC); if anything is missing, the application is deemed to be withdrawn (R. 71(7) EPC).
einheit:e01n94-3b.merke: Approval: fee for grant, claims fees, translations.
einheit:e01n94-3b.abschnitt: R. 71(3) EPC: communication of the intention to grant

einheit:e01n94-3c.frage: Must C pay fees and file translations if he requests correction of the typing error in time?
loesung: **No.** On a reasoned request for correction, the Examining Division, if it consents, issues a new communication under R. 71(3) EPC; otherwise it resumes examination (R. 71(6) EPC). Fees and translations are only due in reply to the new communication (Guidelines C-V, 4.1); the reasoning should address R. 139 EPC (Guidelines C-V, 4.3).
einheit:e01n94-3c.merke: A request for amendment or correction replaces payment in reply to the first communication.
einheit:e01n94-3c.abschnitt: R. 71(3) EPC: communication of the intention to grant

gruppe:e01n94-4.sachverhalt: In reply to the communication under R. 71(3) EPC, D has paid all fees and filed the translations. Two weeks later he learns of an earlier European application that destroys the novelty of claim 1, but not of dependent claim 2. The decision to grant has not yet been issued.

einheit:e01n94-4a.frage: Can D still have claim 1 deleted?
loesung: **Yes.** Until the decision to grant, the Examining Division may resume examination (R. 71a(2) EPC), namely until the decision is handed over to the internal postal service (G 12/91). It admits amendments after approval only exceptionally (R. 137(3) EPC); a deletion that is quickly examinable and allowable speaks in favour (Guidelines H-II, 2.6).
einheit:e01n94-4a.merke: Until handover to the postal service, the grant is not final.
einheit:e01n94-4a.abschnitt: Art. 97 EPC: decision to grant and its effect

einheit:e01n94-4b.frage: Does the patent take effect on the date of the decision to grant?
loesung: **No.** The decision to grant only takes effect on the date on which the mention of the grant is published in the European Patent Bulletin (Art. 97(3) EPC). The opposition period also runs from that date (Art. 99(1) EPC).
einheit:e01n94-4b.merke: Effective with the mention in the Bulletin.
einheit:e01n94-4b.abschnitt: Art. 97 EPC: decision to grant and its effect

einheit:e01n94-4c.frage: Can D still file a divisional application on the date of the mention of grant?
loesung: **No.** The application is only pending up to the day before the mention of grant; R. 134 EPC does not extend this (Guidelines A-IV, 1.1.1). The divisional must be received on the preceding day at the latest (R. 36(1) EPC).
einheit:e01n94-4c.merke: Divisional at the latest on the day before the mention of grant.
einheit:e01n94-4c.abschnitt: Art. 97 EPC: decision to grant and its effect

gruppe:e01n94-5.sachverhalt: The Examining Division had refused EP-E. The Board of Appeal remits the case with an order to grant on the basis of a text it has finally determined. In reply to the communication under R. 71(3) EPC, E only requests an additional dependent claim and pays nothing. The EPO notifies a loss of rights.

einheit:e01n94-5a.frage: Should the Examining Division have issued a new communication under R. 71(3) EPC?
loesung: **No.** The Examining Division is bound by the Board's decision (Art. 111(2) EPC); the procedure under R. 71(6) EPC therefore does not apply. The request for amendment does not replace payment, and the application is deemed to be withdrawn (R. 71(7) EPC; Guidelines E-XI, 9).
einheit:e01n94-5a.merke: Text determined by the Board: no request for amendment under R. 71(6) EPC.
einheit:e01n94-5a.abschnitt: R. 71(6) and 71(7) EPC: after the appeal

einheit:e01n94-5b.frage: Can E still obtain the additional claim in a patent?
loesung: **Yes,** via a divisional application. First EP-E must become pending again: further processing within two months of the communication with the fee, the fee for grant and the translations of the Board's text (Art. 121 EPC, R. 135(1) EPC). Then a divisional with the additional claim (R. 36(1) EPC), without double patenting (G 4/19).
einheit:e01n94-5b.merke: First further processing, then a divisional.
einheit:e01n94-5b.abschnitt: R. 71(6) and 71(7) EPC: after the appeal

kapitel:e01n99.titel: Art. 99 to 101 and 105 EPC: opposition and intervention

einheit:e01n99-0.titel: Who, by when, on which grounds
einheit:e01n99-0.text: Opposition questions come up in Paper D almost every year (2015 Q2, 2017 Q2, 2018 Q2, 2019 Q4, 2022 Q6, 2023 Q3, 2024 Q3 and Q4). Novelty itself is rarely asked; the procedure is: **who** may oppose, **by when** and with which fee (Art. 99(1) EPC), which deficiencies can only be remedied within the opposition period (R. 77 EPC), which **grounds** count (Art. 100 EPC) and how far the Opposition Division examines (G 9/91, G 10/91, G 3/14). Add the transfer of opponent status, continuation of the Office's own motion (R. 84 EPC) and the **intervention** of the assumed infringer (Art. 105 EPC).

gruppe:e01n99-1.sachverhalt: The mention of the grant of patent EP-P of company P is published on 4 June 2025. Patent attorney S files an opposition in his own name on 2 March 2026; in fact he is acting for a competitor that wishes to remain anonymous. The opposition fee is received on 6 March 2026.

einheit:e01n99-1a.frage: Is the opposition inadmissible because S is acting for an undisclosed third party?
loesung: **No.** Any person may oppose (Art. 99(1) EPC), including a straw man acting on behalf of a third party. The opposition would only be inadmissible in case of an abusive circumvention of the law, e.g. if S were in fact acting for the proprietor (G 3/97).
einheit:e01n99-1a.merke: A straw man may oppose, just not for the proprietor.
einheit:e01n99-1a.abschnitt: Art. 99(1) EPC: opponent, time limit, fee

einheit:e01n99-1b.frage: Has the opposition been validly filed?
loesung: **No.** The opposition period ended on 4 March 2026 (first sentence of Art. 99(1) EPC, R. 131(4) EPC). The opposition is only deemed filed once the fee is paid (second sentence of Art. 99(1) EPC); after late payment it is deemed not to have been filed (Guidelines D-IV, 1.2.1). Only the applicant can request further processing (Art. 121(1) EPC), and there is no re-establishment in the opposition period (Guidelines D-III, 1).
einheit:e01n99-1b.merke: No fee within the period, no opposition.
einheit:e01n99-1b.abschnitt: Art. 99(1) EPC: opponent, time limit, fee

einheit:e01n99-1c.frage: Could P itself oppose its own patent to get rid of an overly broad claim?
loesung: **No.** The proprietor is not "any person" within the meaning of Art. 99(1) EPC (G 9/93). Self-limitation is what the limitation procedure under Art. 105a EPC is for.
einheit:e01n99-1c.merke: Against your own patent: limitation, not opposition.
einheit:e01n99-1c.abschnitt: Art. 99(1) EPC: opponent, time limit, fee

einheit:e01n99-1d.frage: Is an opposition then admissible at all?
loesung: **Yes.** An opposition may be filed even if the patent has lapsed for all designated states (R. 75 EPC). Lapse only has effect for the future, revocation from the outset (Art. 68 EPC); claims relating to the period before may persist (Guidelines D-I, 2).
einheit:e01n99-1d.merke: Even a lapsed patent can be attacked.
einheit:e01n99-1d.abwandlung: P had already let the patent lapse in all designated states before the opposition.
einheit:e01n99-1d.abschnitt: Art. 99(1) EPC: opponent, time limit, fee

gruppe:e01n99-2.sachverhalt: Luca, an Italian national resident in Brazil, and Marco, resident in Milan, jointly file an opposition against EP-Q within the opposition period. The notice is in Italian, signed by both and states the extent, grounds, facts and evidence. They pay one opposition fee.

einheit:e01n99-2a.frage: Is a single opposition fee enough?
loesung: **Yes.** An opposition filed jointly by several persons is admissible with one fee (G 3/99; Guidelines D-III, 2). Throughout the proceedings it must be clear who belongs to the group; procedural acts are performed by the common representative (R. 151(1) EPC).
einheit:e01n99-2a.merke: Joint opposition: one fee, one common representative.
einheit:e01n99-2a.abschnitt: R. 76 and 77 EPC: content and deficiencies

einheit:e01n99-2b.frage: Were the two allowed to file the opposition in Italian?
loesung: **Yes.** Marco lives in Italy, Luca is an Italian national resident abroad; both may use Italian (Art. 14(4) EPC). The translation into an official language of the EPO must be filed within one month or by the end of the opposition period, whichever expires later (R. 6(2) EPC).
einheit:e01n99-2b.merke: Italians abroad may file in Italian, with a translation.
einheit:e01n99-2b.abschnitt: R. 76 and 77 EPC: content and deficiencies

einheit:e01n99-2c.frage: Must Luca appoint a professional representative?
loesung: **Yes.** A person having neither residence nor principal place of business in a Contracting State must be represented (Art. 133(2) EPC); nationality does not help. The deficiency can be remedied on invitation within the period set (R. 77(2) EPC); the representative must also sign or approve the notice of opposition (Guidelines D-IV, 1.2.2.2).
einheit:e01n99-2c.merke: Residence outside the Contracting States: representative needed, deficiency remediable.
einheit:e01n99-2c.abschnitt: R. 76 and 77 EPC: content and deficiencies

einheit:e01n99-2d.frage: Will the two be invited to supply the facts and evidence later?
loesung: **No.** The indications under R. 76(2)(c) EPC must be present by the end of the opposition period. If they are still missing then, the Opposition Division rejects the opposition as inadmissible without an invitation (R. 77(1) EPC). An invitation to remedy exists only for the other deficiencies (R. 77(2) EPC).
einheit:e01n99-2d.merke: Grounds, facts, evidence: remediable only until the period ends.
einheit:e01n99-2d.abwandlung: The notice of opposition states no facts and evidence; the two want to supply them after the opposition period has expired.
einheit:e01n99-2d.abschnitt: R. 76 and 77 EPC: content and deficiencies

gruppe:e01n99-3.sachverhalt: EP-N contains independent claim 1 (A), dependent claim 2 (A+B) and independent claim 3 (D). Opponent O attacks only claim 1, for lack of novelty over D1. After the opposition period she files D2, which discloses D. The proprietor defends claim 1 combined with feature B.

einheit:e01n99-3a.frage: Does the Opposition Division examine claim 3 in the light of D2?
loesung: **No.** The statement of the extent of the opposition (R. 76(2)(c) EPC) limits the power to examine; independent claims not attacked are not examined (G 9/91). D2 is therefore irrelevant for claim 3, even if prima facie relevant.
einheit:e01n99-3a.merke: The extent of the opposition limits the examination.
einheit:e01n99-3a.abschnitt: Art. 100 and 101 EPC: grounds and scope of examination

einheit:e01n99-3b.frage: Can O object that the new claim 1 is unclear because granted claim 2 was already unclear?
loesung: **No.** Amended claims are examined for clarity (Art. 84 EPC) only insofar as the amendment introduces the deficiency. Merely incorporating a granted dependent claim does not suffice for that (G 3/14).
einheit:e01n99-3b.merke: Clarity only insofar as the amendment causes the problem.
einheit:e01n99-3b.abschnitt: Art. 100 and 101 EPC: grounds and scope of examination

einheit:e01n99-3c.frage: Could O have raised the lack of clarity of granted claim 2 as a ground for opposition?
loesung: **No.** Art. 100 EPC lists the grounds for opposition exhaustively: lack of patentability, insufficiency of disclosure, added matter. Lack of clarity is not among them. The Opposition Division examines grounds under Art. 100 EPC not raised only exceptionally, if they prima facie prejudice maintenance (G 10/91).
einheit:e01n99-3c.merke: Art. 84 EPC is not a ground for opposition.
einheit:e01n99-3c.abschnitt: Art. 100 and 101 EPC: grounds and scope of examination

gruppe:e01n99-4.sachverhalt: Company E filed an opposition against patent EP-R to protect its pumps business unit. After the opposition period, E sells this business unit to F; the contract expressly also transfers the opposition. A document under Art. 54(3) EPC clearly anticipates claim 1.

loesung: **Yes.** The opposition is not freely transferable (G 2/04), but passes with the business unit in whose interest it was filed (G 4/88). F must prove the transfer by documents; the EPO examines it of its own motion at every stage (T 1178/04).
einheit:e01n99-4a.merke: The opposition follows the business unit, not the contract alone.
einheit:e01n99-4a.abschnitt: R. 84 EPC: opponent status and continuation

einheit:e01n99-4b.titel: Continuation of the Office's own motion
einheit:e01n99-4b.frage: Does the opposition procedure thereby end?
loesung: **No.** The Opposition Division may continue the proceedings of its own motion after withdrawal of the opposition (second sentence of R. 84(2) EPC). It does so where revocation or limitation is likely without further assistance and without extensive investigation, here owing to the clear anticipation (Guidelines D-VII, 5.2 and 5.3).
einheit:e01n99-4b.merke: Withdrawal of the opposition does not necessarily end the proceedings.
einheit:e01n99-4b.abwandlung: F withdraws the opposition shortly afterwards.
einheit:e01n99-4b.abschnitt: R. 84 EPC: opponent status and continuation

einheit:e01n99-4c.frage: Does the Board of Appeal continue the proceedings?
loesung: **No.** If the opponent who is the sole appellant withdraws the opposition, the appeal proceedings end immediately, whatever the Board's view of the legal position (G 8/93). The rejection of the opposition becomes final; the proprietor can only give up the anticipated claim 1 through limitation proceedings (Art. 105a EPC).
einheit:e01n99-4c.merke: On appeal there is no continuation of the Office's own motion.
einheit:e01n99-4c.abwandlung: The withdrawal only occurs on appeal: the Opposition Division had rejected the opposition, and F alone filed an appeal.
einheit:e01n99-4c.abschnitt: R. 84 EPC: opponent status and continuation

gruppe:e01n99-5.titel: The infringement action during the opposition
gruppe:e01n99-5.sachverhalt: An opposition by company C, based only on Art. 100(c) EPC, is pending against company B's EP-B. The opposition period has expired. On 2 March 2026 B sues D for infringement of EP-B. D holds a document under Art. 54(3) EPC that anticipates claim 1.

einheit:e01n99-5a.frage: By when can D intervene in the opposition proceedings?
optionen: not at all, because the opposition period has expired
loesung: **By 2 June 2026.** Notice of intervention must be filed within three months of the date on which infringement proceedings were instituted (Art. 105(1) EPC, R. 89(1) EPC), in writing with reasons; it is only deemed filed once the opposition fee is paid (R. 89(2) EPC).
einheit:e01n99-5a.merke: Intervention: three months from the action, with opposition fee.

einheit:e01n99-5b.frage: May D base the intervention on lack of novelty even though C did not raise this ground?
loesung: **Yes.** An admissible intervention is treated as an opposition (Art. 105(2) EPC) and may be based on any ground for opposition under Art. 100 EPC (G 1/94; Guidelines D-VII, 6). D therefore invokes Art. 100(a) EPC with Art. 54(3) EPC.
einheit:e01n99-5b.merke: The intervener has all grounds for opposition.

einheit:e01n99-5c.frage: Do the appeal proceedings continue with D?
loesung: **No.** Intervention is also admissible in appeal proceedings (G 1/94), but the intervener does not acquire the status of an appellant there. Once all appeals are withdrawn, the proceedings end (G 2/24).
einheit:e01n99-5c.merke: An intervener at the appeal stage depends on the other parties' appeals.
einheit:e01n99-5c.abwandlung: The action is only brought when the case is before the Board of Appeal; D intervenes there. C, the sole appellant, then withdraws the appeal.

kapitel:e01n105a.titel: Art. 105a to 105c EPC, R. 90 to 96 EPC: limitation and revocation

einheit:e01n105a-0.text: In Paper D, limitation is the proprietor's route when opposition no longer helps (2021 Q6, 2022 Q6, 2023 Q3, 2024 Q4). The request can be filed **at any time after grant**, even after the patent has lapsed, but not while opposition proceedings are pending (Art. 105a EPC). An opposition filed later takes precedence over limitation, but not over revocation (R. 93 EPC; Guidelines D-X, 7.1). The Examining Division only examines whether the claims are genuinely limited and whether Art. 84 EPC and Art. 123(2) and 123(3) EPC are complied with (R. 95(2) EPC), not patentability. The decision applies to all Contracting States and takes effect ab initio (Art. 105b(3) EPC, Art. 68 EPC).

gruppe:e01n105a-1.sachverhalt: Company L's patent EP-L was granted in 2019; no opposition was filed. In 2026 L finds a prior publication that anticipates claim 1 but not dependent claim 2. L wants to combine claims 1 and 2.

einheit:e01n105a-1a.frage: Can L still have the patent limited by the EPO?
loesung: **Yes.** The request is not subject to any time limit: it can be filed at any time after grant, even after opposition proceedings (Art. 105a(1) EPC; Guidelines D-X, 1). It is deemed to be filed only when the limitation fee has been paid.
einheit:e01n105a-1a.merke: Limitation: no time limit, but a fee.

einheit:e01n105a-1b.frage: What does L not have to include in the request?
optionen: the complete version of the amended claims
the list of the Contracting States in which the patent has taken effect
reasons why the limited claim is novel over the prior publication
particulars of L as the requester
loesung: **The reasons for novelty.** R. 92(2) EPC requires particulars of the requester, the number of the patent with a list of the states in which it has taken effect, and the complete version of the amended claims. The EPO does not examine why the patent is being limited (Guidelines D-X, 4.3.4).
einheit:e01n105a-1b.merke: The request needs claims, not reasons.

einheit:e01n105a-1c.frage: Does the Examining Division examine whether the limited claim is novel over the prior publication?
loesung: **No.** It only examines whether the amendment is a limitation and complies with Art. 84 EPC and Art. 123(2) and 123(3) EPC (R. 95(2) EPC). Whether L achieves its aim remains open (Guidelines D-X, 4.3.4); L bears the risk.
einheit:e01n105a-1c.merke: No examination of patentability in limitation proceedings.

einheit:e01n105a-1d.frage: Can L still limit the patent?
loesung: **Yes.** Limitation is possible even after the patent has lapsed or expired (Guidelines D-X, 1). It can be worthwhile because under Art. 68 EPC it takes effect ab initio and thus also covers claims relating to the period before the lapse.
einheit:e01n105a-1d.merke: Even a lapsed patent can be limited.
einheit:e01n105a-1d.abwandlung: L has stopped paying the renewal fees; the patent has lapsed in all states.

gruppe:e01n105a-2.sachverhalt: The mention of the grant of EP-M is published on 7 January 2026. On 2 March 2026 the proprietor M requests limitation and pays the fee. On 8 April 2026 W files an admissible opposition.

einheit:e01n105a-2a.frage: Was the request of 2 March 2026 admissible although the opposition period was still running?
loesung: **Yes.** The request is only ruled out while opposition proceedings are **pending** (Art. 105a(2) EPC, R. 93(1) EPC). On 2 March 2026 nobody had filed an opposition; the running opposition period does no harm.
einheit:e01n105a-2a.merke: Only a pending opposition bars the request.
einheit:e01n105a-2a.abschnitt: Art. 105a(2) EPC and R. 93 EPC: precedence of opposition

einheit:e01n105a-2b.frage: Do the limitation proceedings continue after the opposition is filed?
loesung: **No.** The Examining Division terminates the limitation proceedings and orders reimbursement of the limitation fee (R. 93(2) EPC). M can file its amendments in the opposition proceedings (R. 80 EPC).
einheit:e01n105a-2b.abschnitt: Art. 105a(2) EPC and R. 93 EPC: precedence of opposition

einheit:e01n105a-2c.frage: Can M file a new request for limitation during the opposition proceedings?
loesung: **No.** Such a request is deemed not to have been filed; the fee is refunded (R. 93(1) EPC; Guidelines D-X, 2.1). Only once the opposition proceedings are concluded is the route open again.
einheit:e01n105a-2c.abschnitt: Art. 105a(2) EPC and R. 93 EPC: precedence of opposition

einheit:e01n105a-2d.frage: Are revocation proceedings also terminated because of the opposition?
loesung: **No.** R. 93(2) EPC applies only to limitation. The revocation proceedings continue; if the patent is revoked, the opposition ends. Only if the request for revocation is withdrawn, rejected as inadmissible or deemed not to have been filed do the opposition proceedings continue (Guidelines D-X, 7.1).
einheit:e01n105a-2d.merke: Revocation takes precedence over opposition; limitation does not.
einheit:e01n105a-2d.abwandlung: On 2 March 2026 M had requested not limitation but revocation of the patent.
einheit:e01n105a-2d.abschnitt: Art. 105a(2) EPC and R. 93 EPC: precedence of opposition

gruppe:e01n105a-3.sachverhalt: Claim 1 of EP-S reads “beverage with 2 to 8% fruit juice”; the description discloses 2 to 8% apple juice. An earlier Austrian application, published only after the filing date of EP-S, shows a beverage with 4% grape juice. The proprietor wants to limit the patent for Austria only, to “beverage with 2 to 8% apple juice”.

einheit:e01n105a-3a.frage: May the proprietor file separate claims for Austria in limitation proceedings?
loesung: **Yes.** Because of an earlier national right (Art. 139(2) EPC), the patent may contain different claims for that state (R. 138 EPC). The proprietor must inform the EPO of the earlier right; otherwise the request is rejected (Guidelines D-X, 10.1).
einheit:e01n105a-3a.merke: Earlier national right: separate claims for that state.
einheit:e01n105a-3a.abschnitt: R. 95 and 138 EPC: examination and different claims

loesung: **No.** The upper limit of 8% now applies only to apple juice. A beverage with 5% apple juice and 5% grape juice would fall under the new claim but not under the granted one; the protection is extended (Art. 123(3) EPC, R. 95(2) EPC). The Examining Division gives one opportunity to correct the deficiency.
einheit:e01n105a-3b.merke: An apparent limitation can extend the protection.
einheit:e01n105a-3b.abschnitt: R. 95 and 138 EPC: examination and different claims

einheit:e01n105a-3c.frage: May the proprietor then limit the patent for Austria only?
loesung: **No.** Since EPC 2000, earlier European applications are prior art for all Contracting States, irrespective of designations. Different claims cannot be based on them for applications filed on or after 13 December 2007 (Guidelines D-X, 10.1).
einheit:e01n105a-3c.merke: Art. 54(3) EPC applies equally to all states.
einheit:e01n105a-3c.abwandlung: The earlier right is not an Austrian application but an earlier European application designating Austria.
einheit:e01n105a-3c.abschnitt: R. 95 and 138 EPC: examination and different claims

gruppe:e01n105a-4.titel: The claim the opposition did not cover
gruppe:e01n105a-4.sachverhalt: In opposition proceedings against EP-T only claim 1 was attacked; the patent was finally maintained with an amended claim 1. Independent claim 3 is anticipated by a document under Art. 54(3) EPC. The proprietor T wants to delete claim 3.

einheit:e01n105a-4a.frage: Can T now initiate limitation proceedings?
loesung: **Yes.** The opposition proceedings are concluded; Art. 105a(2) EPC no longer stands in the way. The subject of the proceedings is the patent as amended in opposition (R. 90 EPC). Deleting a claim reduces the extent of protection and is a limitation (Guidelines D-X, 4.3.1).
einheit:e01n105a-4a.merke: After opposition, limitation repairs what was not examined there.
einheit:e01n105a-4a.abschnitt: Art. 105b and 105c EPC: decision and effect

einheit:e01n105a-4b.frage: Does the limitation take effect only for the future?
loesung: **No.** To the extent that the patent is limited, it is deemed not to have had the effects specified from the outset (Art. 68 EPC). The decision applies to the patent in all Contracting States and takes effect on publication of its mention in the European Patent Bulletin (Art. 105b(3) EPC).
einheit:e01n105a-4b.merke: Limitation takes effect ex tunc and for all states.
einheit:e01n105a-4b.abschnitt: Art. 105b and 105c EPC: decision and effect

einheit:e01n105a-4c.frage: Does T still have to do anything when the Examining Division communicates that it intends to allow the request?
loesung: **Yes.** Within three months T must file translations of the amended claims into the two other official languages (R. 95(3) EPC); if it fails to do so, it can still do so within two months of a communication on that failure (first sentence of R. 82(3) EPC). The EPO then limits the patent and publishes the amended specification (Art. 105c EPC).
einheit:e01n105a-4c.merke: At the end: translations of the claims within three months.
einheit:e01n105a-4c.abschnitt: Art. 105b and 105c EPC: decision and effect

kapitel:e01n108.titel: Art. 106 to 112a EPC: appeal and petition for review

einheit:e01n108-0.text: On appeals, Paper D mainly asks about the **time limit and fee** (Art. 108 EPC), **reimbursement** of the appeal fee (R. 103 EPC), **entitlement to appeal** (Art. 107 EPC) and remedies for a missed time limit (2016 Q1, 2018 Q4, 2022 Q6, 2023 Q4). The time limit for appeal is excluded from further processing (Art. 121(4) EPC); re-establishment of rights is available to applicants and proprietors, but to the opponent only for the time limit for the grounds (G 1/86). R. 103 EPC staggers reimbursement by the time of withdrawal (100, 75, 50 or 25%). Against decisions of the Boards, only the petition for review remains (Art. 112a EPC).

gruppe:e01n108-1.sachverhalt: The Examining Division refuses A's application at oral proceedings on 9 June 2026. The written decision is dated 23 June 2026 and reaches A on 26 June 2026.

einheit:e01n108-1a.frage: By when must A file the notice of appeal and pay the fee?
loesung: **By 24 August 2026.** The time limit is two months from notification of the written decision (first sentence of Art. 108 EPC). It is deemed notified on 23 June 2026 because it was received within seven days (R. 126(2) EPC). 23 August 2026 is a Sunday; the time limit expires on the Monday (R. 134(1) EPC).
einheit:e01n108-1a.merke: What counts is the written decision, not its pronouncement.
einheit:e01n108-1a.abschnitt: Art. 108 EPC: time limit, fee, grounds

einheit:e01n108-1b.frage: By when must the statement of grounds of appeal be received?
loesung: **By 23 October 2026.** The time limit for filing the grounds is four months from notification of the decision (third sentence of Art. 108 EPC). The extension of the time limit for appeal under R. 134(1) EPC does not carry over; 23 October 2026 is a Friday.
einheit:e01n108-1b.merke: Four months from notification, not from filing the appeal.
einheit:e01n108-1b.abschnitt: Art. 108 EPC: time limit, fee, grounds

loesung: **No,** it is deemed **not to have been filed** because the notice of appeal was not received in time; the fee is reimbursed (G 1/18). Further processing is ruled out for the time limit under Art. 108 EPC (Art. 121(4) EPC); A's only option is re-establishment of rights (Art. 122 EPC).
einheit:e01n108-1c.merke: Notice and fee: both in time, otherwise there is no appeal.
einheit:e01n108-1c.abwandlung: A pays the fee on 20 August 2026 but files the notice of appeal only on 25 August 2026.
einheit:e01n108-1c.abschnitt: Art. 108 EPC: time limit, fee, grounds

gruppe:e01n108-2.sachverhalt: On 10 August 2026 B files an appeal in due time against the refusal of his application and pays the fee. The time limit for the statement of grounds of appeal runs until 23 October 2026. On 1 September 2026 B withdraws the appeal without having filed grounds.

einheit:e01n108-2a.frage: To what extent is the appeal fee reimbursed?
loesung: **In full.** B withdrew the appeal before filing the statement of grounds of appeal and before expiry of the period for filing it (R. 103(1)(b) EPC).
einheit:e01n108-2a.merke: Withdrawal before the grounds: full reimbursement.
einheit:e01n108-2a.abschnitt: R. 103 EPC: reimbursement of the appeal fee

einheit:e01n108-2b.frage: How much does B receive if he withdraws the appeal three weeks after notification of that communication?
loesung: **75%.** The appeal is withdrawn in response to the communication indicating the Board's intention to start substantive examination, within two months of its notification (R. 103(2) EPC). If more than one rate applies, the higher rate applies (R. 103(5) EPC).
einheit:e01n108-2b.merke: Announcement of substantive examination: two months for 75%.
einheit:e01n108-2b.abwandlung: B files the grounds in time. Later the Board communicates that it intends to start substantive examination of the appeal.
einheit:e01n108-2b.abschnitt: R. 103 EPC: reimbursement of the appeal fee

einheit:e01n108-2c.frage: And if B withdraws only four months after that communication, with no oral proceedings scheduled and no time limit set for observations?
loesung: **50%.** The period for filing the grounds has expired, and so has the two-month period under R. 103(2) EPC. With no date for oral proceedings and no invitation to file observations, withdrawal before the decision is issued suffices for 50% (R. 103(3)(c) EPC).
einheit:e01n108-2c.merke: Withdrawn later: 50% until the decision, otherwise 25%.
einheit:e01n108-2c.abschnitt: R. 103 EPC: reimbursement of the appeal fee

gruppe:e01n108-3.sachverhalt: The Examining Division refuses C's application. It did not consider an auxiliary request filed in time which overcomes all objections, because the request had not reached the file. C files an appeal, files grounds and requests reimbursement of the appeal fee.

einheit:e01n108-3a.frage: Must the Examining Division rectify its decision?
loesung: **Yes.** If the department whose decision is contested considers the appeal admissible and well founded, it must rectify its decision (Art. 109(1) EPC), within three months of receipt of the statement of grounds (Art. 109(2) EPC). An overlooked document filed in time is a typical ground for interlocutory revision (Guidelines E-XI, 7.1).
einheit:e01n108-3a.merke: Ex parte proceedings: interlocutory revision within three months.

einheit:e01n108-3b.frage: May the Examining Division rectify its decision and at the same time refuse the request for reimbursement?
loesung: **No.** It orders reimbursement if it considers it equitable by reason of a substantial procedural violation (R. 103(1)(a) EPC, R. 103(6) EPC). If it does not consider it equitable, it refers the request to the Board of Appeal; it may not refuse it (G 3/03).
einheit:e01n108-3b.merke: Refusing reimbursement is a matter for the Board.

einheit:e01n108-3c.frage: May the Opposition Division rectify its decision?
loesung: **No.** Interlocutory revision is ruled out where the appellant is opposed by another party (second sentence of Art. 109(1) EPC). The Opposition Division remits the appeal to the Board. Exception: all oppositions have been withdrawn (Guidelines E-XI, 7.1).
einheit:e01n108-3c.merke: Inter partes proceedings: no interlocutory revision.
einheit:e01n108-3c.abwandlung: Instead of an application, the case concerns a patent revoked by the Opposition Division; the opponent is a party to the proceedings.

gruppe:e01n108-4.sachverhalt: The Opposition Division maintains P's patent in amended form (Art. 101(3)(a) EPC). P wanted the patent as granted, the opponent O wanted revocation. Only O appeals; in the notice of appeal, its representative mistakenly names the parent company Q as appellant.

einheit:e01n108-4a.frage: Can P request in the appeal proceedings that the patent be maintained as granted?
loesung: **No.** Without its own appeal, P is only a party as of right (second sentence of Art. 107 EPC). If the opponent is the sole appellant, it may not be put in a worse position; P can only defend the maintained version, exceptionally with limiting amendments (G 1/99).
einheit:e01n108-4a.merke: Whoever does not appeal cannot ask for more.

einheit:e01n108-4b.frage: Is the appeal lost because Q is not adversely affected?
loesung: **No.** The name of the appellant can be corrected under R. 101(2) EPC if the true intention to appeal on behalf of O can be established from the file or by evidence (G 1/12; R. 139 EPC). O should prove its instructions and the mistake.
einheit:e01n108-4b.merke: Wrong appellant: correction under R. 101(2) EPC.

einheit:e01n108-4c.frage: Could O have requested re-establishment if it had missed the time limit for appeal despite all due care?
loesung: **No.** Under Art. 122(1) EPC, re-establishment is available to applicants and proprietors; an opponent cannot be re-established in the time limit for appeal (T 210/89; Guidelines E-VIII, 3.1.2). If it has filed an appeal, re-establishment in the time limit for the grounds is possible (G 1/86). P as proprietor could have requested it.
einheit:e01n108-4c.merke: Opponent: re-establishment only in the time limit for the grounds.

gruppe:e01n108-5.sachverhalt: The Board of Appeal dismisses D's appeal, relying on a document it introduced only at the oral proceedings without giving D an opportunity to comment. D objects immediately; the Board dismisses the objection. The written decision is dated 14 September 2026.

einheit:e01n108-5a.frage: Can D file a petition for review by the Enlarged Board of Appeal?
loesung: **Yes.** A fundamental violation of the right to be heard (Art. 113 EPC) is a ground for review (Art. 112a(2)(c) EPC). D raised the objection during the appeal proceedings, as R. 106 EPC requires. A merely wrong decision on the merits is not sufficient.
einheit:e01n108-5a.merke: Review only for serious procedural defects, after an objection.

einheit:e01n108-5b.frage: By when must D file the petition and pay the fee?
loesung: **By 16 November 2026.** The time limit is two months from notification of the decision (Art. 112a(4) EPC); 14 November 2026 is a Saturday (R. 134(1) EPC). The petition is deemed filed only once the fee has been paid, and it must state the reasons (R. 107 EPC).
einheit:e01n108-5b.merke: Petition for review: two months, with fee and reasons.

einheit:e01n108-5c.titel: Missed time limit for the petition
einheit:e01n108-5c.frage: Can D remedy a missed time limit for the petition by further processing?
loesung: **No.** The time limit under Art. 112a(4) EPC is excluded from further processing (Art. 121(4) EPC). Re-establishment of rights is possible, requested within two months of expiry of the time limit (second sentence of R. 136(1) EPC). The petition has no suspensive effect (Art. 112a(3) EPC).
einheit:e01n108-5c.merke: As for priority: re-establishment within two months of expiry of the time limit.

kapitel:e01n115.titel: Art. 114 and 115 EPC: third-party observations and examination of its own motion

einheit:e01n115-0.text: Anyone who wants to act against someone else's application without becoming a party files **third-party observations** (Art. 115 EPC): after publication, in writing, in an official language, with reasons, without a fee, even anonymously (R. 114 EPC). Paper D asks whether observations can still hold up the decision to grant (2018 Q5) and which objections are admissible, e.g. lack of clarity (2019 Q2). This is made possible by **examination of its own motion** (Art. 114(1) EPC). Art. 114(2) EPC allows the EPO to disregard late-filed submissions.

gruppe:e01n115-1.titel: The competitor wants to remain anonymous
gruppe:e01n115-1.sachverhalt: N's European application has been published and is in examination. Competitor M has a Japanese patent specification that anticipates claim 1, and considers claim 2 unclear. M does not want N to learn of its action.

einheit:e01n115-1a.frage: Can M file observations without giving its name?
loesung: **Yes.** Third-party observations can be filed anonymously (Guidelines E-VI, 3). They are communicated to N, who may comment on them (R. 114(2) EPC).
einheit:e01n115-1a.merke: Third-party observations: anonymous filing is allowed.

einheit:e01n115-1b.frage: May M file the Japanese patent specification in the original language?
loesung: **Yes.** The observations themselves must be filed in an official language and must state the grounds (R. 114(1) EPC). Evidence such as documents may be filed in any language; the EPO may request a translation (Guidelines E-VI, 3).
einheit:e01n115-1b.merke: Submission in an official language, evidence in any language.

einheit:e01n115-1c.frage: Can M also object to the lack of clarity of claim 2?
loesung: **Yes.** Art. 115 EPC refers to patentability, but the EPO also takes into account objections concerning clarity (Art. 84 EPC), sufficiency of disclosure and unallowable amendments (Guidelines E-VI, 3).
einheit:e01n115-1c.merke: Clarity, too, can be the subject of observations.

einheit:e01n115-1d.frage: Can M already file observations now?
loesung: **No.** Observations can only be filed after publication of the European patent application (first sentence of Art. 115 EPC).
einheit:e01n115-1d.merke: Only publication opens the door to Art. 115 EPC.
einheit:e01n115-1d.abwandlung: N's application has not yet been published; M knows of it from licence negotiations.

gruppe:e01n115-2.sachverhalt: In response to the communication under R. 71(3) EPC, P has paid the fees and filed the translations. Q then files observations citing an earlier European application that anticipates claim 1. The decision to grant has not yet been handed over to the EPO postal service.

einheit:e01n115-2a.frage: Must the Examining Division still take the observations into account?
loesung: **Yes.** Observations received after the communication under R. 71(3) EPC but before the decision to grant is handed over to the EPO postal service are considered; if they are relevant, the Examining Division resumes examination (Guidelines E-VI, 3).
einheit:e01n115-2a.merke: Until handover to the postal service, every observation counts.
einheit:e01n115-2a.abschnitt: Art. 115 EPC: consideration and legal status

einheit:e01n115-2b.frage: Are the observations then still taken into account?
loesung: **No.** Handover to the EPO postal service concludes the written proceedings (G 12/91). Observations received later are added to the file without being considered (Guidelines E-VI, 3).
einheit:e01n115-2b.merke: After handover to the postal service: added to the file only.
einheit:e01n115-2b.abwandlung: The observations are received one day after the decision to grant has been handed over to the EPO postal service.
einheit:e01n115-2b.abschnitt: Art. 115 EPC: consideration and legal status

einheit:e01n115-2c.frage: Can Q appeal against the decision to grant?
loesung: **No.** The third party is not a party to the proceedings (second sentence of Art. 115 EPC); only parties are entitled to appeal (Art. 107 EPC). Q can still file an opposition within nine months of the mention of the grant (Art. 99(1) EPC).
einheit:e01n115-2c.merke: No party, no appeal – but opposition.
einheit:e01n115-2c.abschnitt: Art. 115 EPC: consideration and legal status

gruppe:e01n115-3.sachverhalt: R's patent has been granted; the opposition period is running and no opposition has yet been filed. S files observations: R showed the invention at an in-house trade fair before the filing date. S does not enclose any evidence.

einheit:e01n115-3a.frage: Does the EPO take the observations into account now?
loesung: **No.** Observations received while no proceedings are pending are not taken into account. They are considered once proceedings become pending again, e.g. opposition or limitation proceedings (Guidelines E-VI, 3).

einheit:e01n115-3b.frage: Must the Opposition Division base its decision on the prior use if R disputes it?
loesung: **No.** Alleged prior art that does not result from a document, such as a use, is only taken into account if it is undisputed or proven beyond reasonable doubt (Guidelines E-VI, 3).
einheit:e01n115-3b.merke: Prior use from observations: undisputed or proven.
einheit:e01n115-3b.abwandlung: In the meantime a third party has filed an opposition; S's observations are before the Opposition Division.

gruppe:e01n115-4.titel: Examination of its own motion in opposition
gruppe:e01n115-4.sachverhalt: T files an opposition against U's patent, based only on lack of novelty over D1. The Opposition Division additionally considers that the claims contain added matter.

einheit:e01n115-4a.frage: May the Opposition Division examine the ground of added matter, which was not invoked?
loesung: **Yes,** exceptionally: under Art. 114(1) EPC it may go beyond the opposition if the fresh ground prima facie prejudices maintenance of the patent (G 10/91; Guidelines E-VI, 2.1).
einheit:e01n115-4a.merke: Fresh ground of its own motion only if prima facie relevant.
einheit:e01n115-4a.abschnitt: Art. 114 EPC: examination of its own motion and late filing

einheit:e01n115-4b.frage: Must the Opposition Division take into account a document that T submits only at the oral proceedings?
loesung: **No.** The EPO need not take into account facts or evidence not submitted in due time (Art. 114(2) EPC). It admits them only if they are prima facie relevant, i.e. would change the decision (Guidelines E-VI, 2).
einheit:e01n115-4b.merke: Late-filed: admitted only if prima facie relevant.
einheit:e01n115-4b.abschnitt: Art. 114 EPC: examination of its own motion and late filing

einheit:e01n115-4c.frage: Can the Opposition Division continue the proceedings if T withdraws the opposition?
loesung: **Yes.** After withdrawal of the opposition, the opposition proceedings can be continued by the EPO of its own motion (second sentence of R. 84(2) EPC); this follows from examination of its own motion (Art. 114(1) EPC).
einheit:e01n115-4c.merke: Once filed, the opposition no longer belongs to the opponent alone.
einheit:e01n115-4c.abschnitt: Art. 114 EPC: examination of its own motion and late filing

einheit:e01n115-4d.frage: Can T introduce the fresh ground for opposition for the first time in appeal proceedings if U objects?
loesung: **No.** Fresh grounds for opposition may be examined in appeal proceedings only with the consent of the patent proprietor (G 10/91).
einheit:e01n115-4d.merke: Appeal: fresh ground for opposition only with the proprietor's consent.
einheit:e01n115-4d.abschnitt: Art. 114 EPC: examination of its own motion and late filing

kapitel:e01n120.titel: Art. 120 EPC, R. 126, 127, 131 and 134 EPC: time limits and notification

einheit:e01n120-0.text: Almost every Paper D question requires a time-limit calculation, expressly e.g. in 2016, 2019 and 2022. Art. 120 EPC refers to the Implementing Regulations: determine the event (R. 131(2) EPC), end a month period on the day with the same number or the last day of the month (R. 131(4) EPC), then extend if a filing office is closed or mail is dislocated (R. 134 EPC). **Caution, new law:** since 1 November 2023 a document is deemed notified on the date it bears (R. 126(2) EPC, R. 127(2) EPC). The ten-day rule of older model answers has been abolished; if a document is received more than seven days after its date, the time limit is extended only by the excess days.

gruppe:e01n120-1.sachverhalt: The Examining Division refuses F's application. The decision is dated 3 June 2026 and is notified electronically to the MyEPO mailbox of F's representative. She opens the mailbox only on 5 June 2026.

einheit:e01n120-1a.frage: When is the decision deemed to be notified?
loesung: **On 3 June 2026.** The electronic document is deemed notified on the date it bears (R. 127(2) EPC). Opening the mailbox is irrelevant; the ten-day fiction no longer exists since 1 November 2023 (Guidelines E-II, 2.3).
einheit:e01n120-1a.merke: Notified on the date of the document.

einheit:e01n120-1b.frage: By when must F file the notice of appeal and pay the appeal fee?
loesung: **By 3 August 2026.** The time limit for appeal is two months from notification (first sentence of Art. 108 EPC) and ends on the day with the same number (R. 131(4) EPC). 3 August 2026 is a Monday.

einheit:e01n120-1c.frage: Does the time limit for the statement of grounds of appeal run from the filing of the appeal?
loesung: **No.** The grounds must be filed within four months of notification of the decision (third sentence of Art. 108 EPC). The time limit ends on 3 October 2026, a Saturday, and is extended to Monday, 5 October 2026 (R. 134(1) EPC).
einheit:e01n120-1c.merke: Grounds: four months from notification, not from filing the appeal.

einheit:e01n120-1d.frage: Is the time limit for appeal extended?
loesung: **Yes,** by two days to 5 August 2026. If a document is proven to have been received more than seven days after its date, the time limit expires later by the number of excess days (R. 126(2) EPC). 12 June is nine days after 3 June, i.e. two days too many.
einheit:e01n120-1d.merke: Seven days are covered; each further day extends the time limit.
einheit:e01n120-1d.abwandlung: The decision is sent by registered letter and is proven to have been received only on 12 June 2026.

gruppe:e01n120-2.titel: The communication from the end of the month
gruppe:e01n120-2.sachverhalt: The Examining Division issues a communication under Art. 94(3) EPC dated 31 October 2025, setting a time limit of four months. G needs more time for comparative tests.

einheit:e01n120-2a.frage: When does the time limit expire?
loesung: **On 2 March 2026.** February has no 31st day; the time limit expires on the last day of the month, 28 February 2026 (R. 131(4) EPC). That is a Saturday, on which the filing offices are closed; the time limit extends to Monday, 2 March 2026 (R. 134(1) EPC).
einheit:e01n120-2a.merke: Last day of the month, then check for the weekend.
einheit:e01n120-2a.abschnitt: R. 131 and 132 EPC: calculation and extension

einheit:e01n120-2b.frage: On 20 February 2026 G requests a two-month extension without giving reasons. Until when does the extended time limit run?
loesung: **Until 30 April 2026.** Time limits specified by the EPO may be extended upon request filed before expiry (R. 132(2) EPC). The extended time limit is calculated from the start of the original one: six months from 31 October 2025. Up to two months, and no more than six months in total, are normally granted even without reasons (Guidelines E-VIII, 1.6.1).
einheit:e01n120-2b.merke: An extension is calculated from the start of the original time limit.
einheit:e01n120-2b.abschnitt: R. 131 and 132 EPC: calculation and extension

einheit:e01n120-2c.titel: Chain of time limits: renewal fee
einheit:e01n120-2c.frage: Does the time limit for payment with the additional fee only expire on 1 December 2026?
loesung: **No.** The six-month period under R. 51(2) EPC starts on the due date, even if that is a Sunday, and runs from month end to month end (J 4/91; Guidelines A-X, 5.2.4). It expires on 30 November 2026, a Monday; R. 134 EPC applies only to its end.
einheit:e01n120-2c.merke: Chains of time limits: extending one time limit does not shift the start of the next.
einheit:e01n120-2c.abwandlung: The renewal fee for G's application fell due on 31 May 2026, a Sunday; G has not paid it.
einheit:e01n120-2c.abschnitt: R. 131 and 132 EPC: calculation and extension

gruppe:e01n120-3.sachverhalt: The time limit for H's reply expires on Monday, 27 April 2026. On that day the filing office in The Hague is closed for Koningsdag; Munich and Berlin are open. H files the reply online on 28 April 2026.

einheit:e01n120-3a.titel: Closing day of a filing office
loesung: **Yes.** If even one of the filing offices in Munich, The Hague or Berlin is closed, the time limit extends to the next day on which all are open (R. 134(1) EPC, R. 35(1) EPC). Where and how H files is irrelevant; the EPO publishes the closing days in the Official Journal.
einheit:e01n120-3a.merke: One closed filing office extends the time limit for everyone.

einheit:e01n120-3b.frage: Can H still file the European application claiming priority on 28 April 2026?
loesung: **Yes.** R. 134 EPC applies to all time limits under the Convention, including the priority period under Art. 87(1) EPC, the opposition period and the time limit for entry into the European phase (Guidelines E-VIII, 1.6.2.3).
einheit:e01n120-3b.merke: The priority period, too, is extended under R. 134 EPC.
einheit:e01n120-3b.abwandlung: The priority period for H's subsequent application expires on 27 April 2026.

einheit:e01n120-3c.frage: Is the time limit extended if all filing offices are open but online filing is unavailable for five hours due to announced maintenance?
loesung: **Yes.** Under the second sentence of R. 134(1) EPC, the extension applies mutatis mutandis if a permitted means of electronic filing is unavailable. For planned maintenance this applies from four hours; shorter outages announced at least two working days in advance do not extend the time limit (Guidelines E-VIII, 1.6.2.1).
einheit:e01n120-3c.merke: An online filing outage counts like a closed filing office.

gruppe:e01n120-4.sachverhalt: The time limit for J's statement of grounds of appeal expires on 15 September 2026. J's representative has his place of business in Contracting State P. The EPO announces that mail delivery in P was generally dislocated from 10 to 21 September 2026.

einheit:e01n120-4a.frage: By when can J file the grounds?
loesung: **By 22 September 2026.** If a time limit expires during a general dislocation of mail in a Contracting State, it extends to the first day after the end of the dislocation for parties resident in that state or with a representative there (R. 134(2) EPC). The EPO publishes the beginning and end (R. 134(4) EPC).
einheit:e01n120-4a.merke: General dislocation: time limit until the first day after it ends.

einheit:e01n120-4b.frage: May J rely on the published extension?
loesung: **Yes.** Parties need not question announcements under R. 134(4) EPC without cause. Under the principle of protection of legitimate expectations, they may rely on them even if there was in fact no general dislocation (J 10/20).
einheit:e01n120-4b.merke: Parties may rely on EPO announcements.
einheit:e01n120-4b.abwandlung: It later turns out that the mail in P was running normally; the announcement was based on a misjudgement.

einheit:e01n120-4c.frage: Can the grounds be deemed filed in time?
loesung: **Yes,** on request with evidence (R. 134(5) EPC): an exceptional occurrence dislocated the mail at the representative's locality on one of the last ten days before expiry, and J mailed the grounds no later than the fifth day after the end of the dislocation, 25 September 2026 (Guidelines E-VIII, 1.6.2.2).
einheit:e01n120-4c.merke: Individual dislocation: evidence, last ten days, mailing within five days.
einheit:e01n120-4c.abwandlung: There is no announcement. A flood paralyses the mail at the firm's location from 11 to 20 September 2026; J mails the grounds on 24 September 2026.

kapitel:e01n121.titel: Art. 121 EPC, R. 135 EPC: further processing

einheit:e01n121-0.titel: The standard remedy for missed time limits
einheit:e01n121-0.text: If the applicant has failed to observe a time limit vis-à-vis the EPO, **further processing** is the first thing to consider: pay the fee and complete the omitted act within **two months of the communication** of the loss of rights (R. 135(1) EPC); fault is not examined. Paper D mainly tests the **exclusions**: Art. 121(4) EPC (priority, appeal, review, the time limits for the remedies themselves) and the list in R. 135(2) EPC. There, only re-establishment of rights helps (Art. 122 EPC).

gruppe:e01n121-1.sachverhalt: On 10 February 2026 the Examining Division issues a communication under Art. 94(3) EPC setting a time limit of four months. The applicant G does not reply. The EPO issues a communication under R. 112(1) EPC dated 15 July 2026 stating that the application is deemed to be withdrawn.

loesung: **Yes.** The time limit for replying to a communication is a time limit vis-à-vis the EPO (Art. 94(4) EPC) and is excluded neither by Art. 121(4) EPC nor by R. 135(2) EPC.
einheit:e01n121-1a.merke: Time limits in examination communications allow further processing.

einheit:e01n121-1b.frage: By when must G file the request?
loesung: **By 15 September 2026.** The time limit is two months from the communication of the loss of rights (R. 135(1) EPC). The communication is deemed notified on 15 July 2026 (R. 126(2) EPC); the time limit expires on the day with the same number (R. 131(4) EPC).
einheit:e01n121-1b.merke: Two months from the communication, without ten extra days.

einheit:e01n121-1c.frage: Is it enough to pay only the further processing fee within the time limit and to file the reply later?
loesung: **No.** The omitted act must be completed within the time limit for the request (second sentence of R. 135(1) EPC). If the reply is missing when the time limit expires, the request is inadmissible.
einheit:e01n121-1c.merke: Fee and omitted act – both within the time limit.

gruppe:e01n121-2.sachverhalt: H files a US application on 3 March 2025. Because of a calendar error, he files the subsequent European application only on 5 March 2026, claiming the US priority.

einheit:e01n121-2a.frage: Can H save the priority period by further processing?
loesung: **No.** The time limit under Art. 87(1) EPC is expressly excluded from further processing (Art. 121(4) EPC).

**Yes,** re-establishment of rights in respect of the priority period: request within two months of its expiry, because of the Sunday by 4 May 2026 (R. 134(1) EPC), with fee and reasons (R. 136(1) EPC). It is allowable only if H was unable to observe the period in spite of all due care (Art. 122(1) EPC).
einheit:e01n121-2b.merke: Priority missed: re-establishment within two months of expiry of the period.

gruppe:e01n121-3.sachverhalt: The renewal fee for the third year of J's application fell due on 31 January 2026. J pays neither the fee nor the additional fee by 31 July 2026. The EPO then informs him that the application is deemed to be withdrawn.

loesung: **No.** The grace period for paying renewal fees with an additional fee (R. 51(2) EPC) is one of the time limits excluded by R. 135(2) EPC.

einheit:e01n121-3b.frage: Can J still file a divisional application while the time limit for re-establishment is running?
loesung: **No.** An application deemed to be withdrawn is not pending during the time limit for requesting re-establishment (J 4/11); only successful re-establishment restores pendency (R. 36(1) EPC).
einheit:e01n121-3b.merke: No divisional from a deemed-withdrawn application.

gruppe:e01n121-4.sachverhalt: K receives the communication under R. 71(3) EPC but misses the four-month time limit for the fee for grant and the translation of the claims. The EPO communicates that the application is deemed to be withdrawn (R. 71(7) EPC).

loesung: **Yes.** The time limit under R. 71(3) EPC is not excluded. Within two months of the communication, K pays the further processing fee and completes the payment of the fee for grant and the filing of the translation (R. 135(1) EPC).
einheit:e01n121-4a.merke: R. 71(3) EPC: further processing is available.

einheit:e01n121-4b.frage: Can K file amendments to the claims together with the request for further processing?
loesung: **Yes,** the omitted act is then the request for amendment or correction under R. 71(6) EPC; if the Examining Division consents, it issues a new communication under R. 71(3) EPC, otherwise it resumes examination (Guidelines C-V, 3).
einheit:e01n121-4b.merke: Amendments are still possible with further processing.

kapitel:e01n122.titel: Art. 122 EPC, R. 136 EPC: re-establishment of rights

einheit:e01n122-0.titel: The rescue route with a due-care test
einheit:e01n122-0.text: Re-establishment of rights helps where further processing is ruled out or its time limit has already expired (R. 136(3) EPC). Paper D asks about it regularly: the priority period in 2015 and 2021, the time limit for appeal of proprietor and opponent in 2018, the missed time limit for further processing in 2022 and 2024. Check: **availability** (direct loss of rights, applicant or proprietor), **time limit** (two months from removal of the cause of non-compliance, at most one year; priority: two months from expiry of the period, R. 136(1) EPC), **form** (fee, reasons, omitted act, R. 136(2) EPC) and **all due care** (Art. 122(1) EPC). Art. 122(5) EPC protects third parties who used the invention in good faith in the interim.

gruppe:e01n122-1.sachverhalt: K did not reply to a communication under Art. 94(3) EPC. The communication of the loss of rights under R. 112(1) EPC is dated 2 March 2026. In spite of all due care, K learns of it only on 8 June 2026.

einheit:e01n122-1a.frage: Can K request re-establishment in respect of the time limit for replying to the communication?
loesung: **No.** Further processing is available for that time limit; such time limits are excluded from re-establishment (R. 136(3) EPC). However, K has also missed the time limit for further processing, which expired on 4 May 2026 (2 May was a Saturday). K can request re-establishment in respect of **that** time limit (Guidelines E-VIII, 3.1.1).
einheit:e01n122-1a.merke: Re-establishment in the further processing time limit, not in the original one.
einheit:e01n122-1a.abschnitt: R. 136(1) to 136(3) EPC: availability, time limit and form

einheit:e01n122-1b.frage: By when must K file the request?
loesung: **By 10 August 2026.** The time limit is two months from removal of the cause of non-compliance, here K's knowledge on 8 June 2026 (R. 136(1) EPC). 8 August 2026 is a Saturday, hence the Monday (R. 134(1) EPC). The limit of one year from expiry of the missed time limit is observed.
einheit:e01n122-1b.merke: Two months from removal of the cause, at most one year.
einheit:e01n122-1b.abschnitt: R. 136(1) to 136(3) EPC: availability, time limit and form

einheit:e01n122-1c.frage: Is it enough to file the request and pay the fee for re-establishment by then?
loesung: **No.** The request must state the grounds and set out the facts relied on, completely and at once (R. 136(2) EPC; J 6/22). The omitted act must be completed: the request for further processing, with the fee and the reply to the communication (R. 135(1) EPC).
einheit:e01n122-1c.merke: Fee, reasons and omitted act, all within the time limit for the request.
einheit:e01n122-1c.abschnitt: R. 136(1) to 136(3) EPC: availability, time limit and form

einheit:e01n122-1d.frage: A renewal fee would have fallen due in the meantime. Must K pay it with the request?
loesung: **No.** A renewal fee that would have fallen due between the loss of rights and notification of the decision on re-establishment falls due only on that notification and can be paid within four months thereafter without an additional fee (R. 51(4) EPC).
einheit:e01n122-1d.merke: Renewal fees after the loss of rights: due only upon re-establishment.
einheit:e01n122-1d.abschnitt: R. 136(1) to 136(3) EPC: availability, time limit and form

gruppe:e01n122-2.titel: The assistant and the docketing system
gruppe:e01n122-2.sachverhalt: The Examining Division refuses L's application by decision of 9 March 2026. Representative M has time limits entered by an experienced, carefully selected and regularly supervised assistant. Exceptionally, the assistant forgets the time limit for appeal; M notices this on 15 June 2026.

einheit:e01n122-2a.frage: Does the assistant's error preclude re-establishment in respect of the time limit for appeal?
loesung: **No.** A representative may delegate routine tasks such as noting time limits. Errors of the assistant are not imputed to the representative if the assistant was carefully selected, instructed and supervised (J 5/80; Guidelines E-VIII, 3.2). An isolated mistake in an otherwise satisfactory system suffices.

einheit:e01n122-2b.frage: Is it enough for the request to state that there was an isolated mistake in a well-functioning system?
loesung: **No.** The request must set out the specific facts: the cause, when it arose and when it was removed, and how the docketing system works (R. 136(2) EPC; Guidelines E-VIII, 3.1.4). After expiry of the time limit for the request, M may only clarify, not add new facts (J 6/22).

einheit:e01n122-2c.frage: Can M rely on an isolated mistake in a satisfactory system?
loesung: **No,** as a rule not. The case law on isolated mistakes does not excuse the representative's own omission in the absence of special circumstances (T 1095/06). Full due care is required of the representative personally.
einheit:e01n122-2c.merke: The representative's own omission weighs more heavily.
einheit:e01n122-2c.abwandlung: M had noted the time limit herself but forgot to send the finished notice of appeal.

gruppe:e01n122-3.sachverhalt: The Opposition Division maintains N's patent in amended form. Proprietor N and opponent O are both adversely affected. Because of isolated mistakes, neither files an appeal; both notice this after the time limit for appeal has expired.

einheit:e01n122-3a.frage: Can N request re-establishment in respect of the time limit for appeal?
loesung: **Yes.** Art. 122(1) EPC is open to the patent proprietor. The time limit for appeal is excluded from further processing (Art. 121(4) EPC), so re-establishment is the correct remedy. Within the time limit for the request, N files the notice of appeal and pays the appeal fee (R. 136(2) EPC).
einheit:e01n122-3a.merke: Time limit for appeal: re-establishment only.
einheit:e01n122-3a.abschnitt: Art. 122(1) EPC: who can request re-establishment

einheit:e01n122-3b.titel: Opponent and time limit for appeal
einheit:e01n122-3b.frage: Can O also request re-establishment in respect of the time limit for filing the appeal?
loesung: **No.** Art. 122(1) EPC names only applicants and patent proprietors. An opponent who has not filed an appeal cannot be re-established in the time limit for appeal (T 210/89; Guidelines E-VIII, 3.1.2).
einheit:e01n122-3b.merke: Opponent: no re-establishment in the time limit for appeal.
einheit:e01n122-3b.abschnitt: Art. 122(1) EPC: who can request re-establishment

einheit:e01n122-3c.titel: Opponent and time limit for the grounds
loesung: **Yes.** An opponent who has filed an appeal can be re-established in the time limit for the statement of grounds of appeal (G 1/86). Only the time limit for filing the appeal remains excluded (T 210/89; Guidelines E-VIII, 3.1.2).
einheit:e01n122-3c.merke: Opponent: re-establishment only in the time limit for the grounds.
einheit:e01n122-3c.abwandlung: O filed the appeal in time but missed the time limit for the grounds.
einheit:e01n122-3c.abschnitt: Art. 122(1) EPC: who can request re-establishment

gruppe:e01n122-4.titel: The forgotten renewal fee and the imitator
gruppe:e01n122-4.sachverhalt: The renewal fee for P's published application fell due on 31 March 2026. By mistake, P pays it neither then nor with the additional fee by 30 September 2026. In November 2026 Q starts manufacturing the invention in good faith in Germany, a designated state. P is later re-established.

einheit:e01n122-4a.frage: Could P have requested re-establishment in respect of the time limit under R. 51(1) EPC as early as April 2026?
loesung: **No.** Missing the due date does not directly cause a loss of rights, because payment with an additional fee is still possible (R. 51(2) EPC; Guidelines E-VIII, 3.1.1). Re-establishment only comes into question for the grace period, which expired on 30 September 2026.
einheit:e01n122-4a.merke: No direct loss of rights, no re-establishment.

einheit:e01n122-4b.frage: Must P pay the renewal fee together with the additional fee with the request?
loesung: **Yes.** The omitted act must be completed within the time limit for the request (R. 136(2) EPC); the omitted act is payment of the renewal fee with the additional fee. In addition, the fee for re-establishment must be paid (R. 136(1) EPC).
einheit:e01n122-4b.merke: Omitted act: renewal fee with additional fee.

einheit:e01n122-4c.frage: May Q continue manufacturing after re-establishment?
loesung: **Yes.** Anyone who, in a designated state, has in good faith begun using the invention between the loss of rights and publication of the mention of re-establishment may continue such use without payment in the course of their business or for its needs (Art. 122(5) EPC). The loss of rights occurred at the end of 30 September 2026.
einheit:e01n122-4c.merke: Intervening users keep a right of continued use.

gruppe:e01n122-5.sachverhalt: R, an individual inventor resident in Munich, files an application with the DPMA on 15 April 2025. From 1 April 2026 he is suddenly seriously ill and unable to act; he has no representative. On 20 April 2026 he files the European application claiming the German priority.

einheit:e01n122-5a.titel: Time limit for the request: priority
einheit:e01n122-5a.frage: By when must R request re-establishment in respect of the priority period?
loesung: **By 15 June 2026.** For the priority period, the time limit for the request is two months from expiry of that period (second sentence of R. 136(1) EPC), not from removal of the cause of non-compliance. The priority period expired on 15 April 2026 (Art. 87(1) EPC).
einheit:e01n122-5a.merke: Priority: two months from expiry of the priority period.
einheit:e01n122-5a.abschnitt: Second sentence of R. 136(1) EPC: priority period

einheit:e01n122-5b.frage: Can a sudden serious illness justify re-establishment?
loesung: **Yes,** as an exceptional circumstance (Guidelines E-VIII, 3.2). However, R must show that he otherwise took all due care, e.g. that he was unable to arrange for someone to act for him. The standard is the due care required by the circumstances (Art. 122(1) EPC).
einheit:e01n122-5b.merke: Exceptional circumstances: illness yes, but show precautions.
einheit:e01n122-5b.abschnitt: Second sentence of R. 136(1) EPC: priority period

einheit:e01n122-5c.frage: Does the European application become ineffective if re-establishment fails?
loesung: **No.** It keeps its date of filing of 20 April 2026, only without priority. The relevant date for the state of the art is then the date of filing; everything made available to the public before that date can be cited against it (Art. 89 EPC, Art. 54(2) EPC).
einheit:e01n122-5c.merke: Without priority, the date of filing counts.
einheit:e01n122-5c.abschnitt: Second sentence of R. 136(1) EPC: priority period

einheit:e01n123-0.text: Art. 123 EPC answers three questions. **When** may amendments be made (Art. 123(1) EPC with R. 137 EPC)? **What** may be added: only what the application as filed discloses directly and unambiguously (Art. 123(2) EPC, gold standard under G 2/10). **How far** after grant: no extension of the protection conferred (Art. 123(3) EPC). Paper D tests intermediate generalisation and unsearched subject-matter (2023 Question 1), use claims (2023 Question 6, G 2/88), Art. 123(3) EPC in limitation (2021 Question 6) and amendments in opposition (2018 Question 2). Add disclaimers (G 1/03, G 2/10, G 1/16), the G 1/93 trap and adaptation of the description (G 1/25).

gruppe:e01n123-1.sachverhalt: V files an application directly with the EPO with claims to device A. The description also describes a process with features E and F which shares no common inventive concept with A and is not searched.

einheit:e01n123-1a.frage: May V amend the claims before receiving the search report?
loesung: **No.** Before receiving the European search report, the applicant may not amend the description, claims or drawings unless otherwise provided (R. 137(1) EPC).
einheit:e01n123-1a.merke: No amendments before the search report.

einheit:e01n123-1b.frage: May V amend of his own volition in his reply to the search opinion?
loesung: **Yes.** In reply to the communication under R. 70a EPC, the applicant may amend of his own volition (R. 137(2) EPC; second sentence of Art. 123(1) EPC). Any further amendment requires the consent of the Examining Division (R. 137(3) EPC).
einheit:e01n123-1b.merke: Once of his own volition, then only with consent.

einheit:e01n123-1c.frage: May V replace the claims with claims to the process with E and F?
loesung: **No.** Amended claims may not relate to unsearched subject-matter which does not combine with the originally claimed invention to form a single general inventive concept (R. 137(5) EPC). V must file a divisional application for it while the application is pending (Art. 76 EPC, R. 36(1) EPC).

einheit:e01n123-1d.titel: After the communication under R. 71(3) EPC
einheit:e01n123-1d.frage: Once V has approved the text under R. 71(3) EPC, does he still have a right to further amendments?
loesung: **No.** From then on, the Examining Division admits amendments only at its discretion (R. 137(3) EPC), as a rule only minor ones that do not require examination to be reopened (G 7/93; Guidelines H-II, 2.6).

gruppe:e01n123-2.sachverhalt: W's application describes only one embodiment: a filter with housing G, membrane M and holder H, which clamps M in the housing. It states that the filter may "preferably" have a pressure sensor S. Claim 1 reads "Filter with housing G".

einheit:e01n123-2a.frage: Which standard applies to amendments under Art. 123(2) EPC?
optionen: What is obvious to the skilled person in view of the application
What is supported by the wording of the application
What the skilled person derives directly and unambiguously from the application
loesung: **Direct and unambiguous disclosure.** Only what the skilled person, using common general knowledge, derives directly and unambiguously from the application as filed, explicitly or implicitly, is allowable (gold standard, G 2/10).
einheit:e01n123-2a.merke: Gold standard: directly and unambiguously disclosed.
einheit:e01n123-2a.abschnitt: Art. 123(2) EPC: gold standard and intermediate generalisation

einheit:e01n123-2b.frage: May W add membrane M to claim 1 without holder H?
loesung: **No.** A feature may be isolated from an embodiment only if it is not structurally and functionally linked to the other features. M and H work together; M alone would be an unallowable intermediate generalisation (Guidelines H-V, 3.2.1).
einheit:e01n123-2b.abschnitt: Art. 123(2) EPC: gold standard and intermediate generalisation

einheit:e01n123-2c.frage: May W add pressure sensor S alone to claim 1?
