loesung: **Yes.** S is described generally as preferred and is not linked to M or H. The disclosure justifies combining S in isolation with the housing (Art. 123(2) EPC; Guidelines H-V, 3.2.1).
einheit:e01n123-2c.merke: Independent, generally described feature: may be added in isolation.
einheit:e01n123-2c.abschnitt: Art. 123(2) EPC: gold standard and intermediate generalisation

einheit:e01n123-2d.frage: Must W adapt the description if it still presents S as more than merely preferred and the claim thereby becomes unclear?
loesung: **Yes.** If an amendment of the claims leads to an inconsistency with the description such that, for example, Art. 84 EPC is not met, the description must be adapted (G 1/25).
einheit:e01n123-2d.merke: Inconsistency with consequences under Art. 84 EPC: adapt the description.
einheit:e01n123-2d.abschnitt: Art. 123(2) EPC: gold standard and intermediate generalisation

gruppe:e01n123-3.sachverhalt: Claim 1 of X's application relates to an adhesive with 1 to 10 % of resin Z; the application mentions no specific value. An article on adhesives for the same purpose, published before the date of filing, discloses an adhesive with 5 % Z.

einheit:e01n123-3a.frage: May X restore novelty with the undisclosed disclaimer "excluding 5 % Z"?
loesung: **No.** Under Art. 54(2) EPC, an undisclosed disclaimer may only exclude an **accidental** anticipation (G 1/03). An article for the same purpose is not accidental; X must delimit the claim in another way.
einheit:e01n123-3a.merke: An undisclosed disclaimer does not help against genuine prior art.

loesung: **Yes.** An anticipation is accidental if it is so unrelated that the skilled person would never have taken it into consideration. The disclaimer must not make a technical contribution (G 1/03, G 1/16).
einheit:e01n123-3b.abwandlung: The article concerns a lubricant for drill heads in which Z happens to occur at 5 %.

einheit:e01n123-3c.frage: May X instead disclaim "excluding 4 to 6 % Z"?
loesung: **No.** The disclaimer may not remove more than is necessary to restore novelty (G 1/16, G 1/03).
einheit:e01n123-3c.merke: Disclaimer: as narrow as the anticipation.

einheit:e01n123-3d.frage: Is the disclaimer allowable merely because the application mentions the excluded value?
loesung: **No.** A disclosed disclaimer also infringes Art. 123(2) EPC if the **remaining** subject-matter is not directly and unambiguously disclosed (G 2/10).
einheit:e01n123-3d.merke: For a disclosed disclaimer, what remains is decisive.
einheit:e01n123-3d.abwandlung: The application expressly mentions 5 % Z as an example.

gruppe:e01n123-4.sachverhalt: Claim 1 of Y's granted patent reads "Foodstuff containing 1 to 5 % meat"; the description mentions beef. Y requests limitation to "Foodstuff containing 1 to 5 % beef".

einheit:e01n123-4a.frage: Is the amendment compatible with Art. 123(3) EPC?
loesung: **No.** A foodstuff with 3 % beef and 3 % pork would fall within the new claim but not within the granted one (6 % meat). Narrowing a component of an open composition can extend the protection (Guidelines H-IV, 3.4; T 287/11).
einheit:e01n123-4a.merke: A narrower component in an open composition can extend protection.
einheit:e01n123-4a.abschnitt: Art. 123(3) EPC: extent of protection after grant

einheit:e01n123-4b.frage: Would "1 to 5 % meat, wherein the meat is beef" be allowable?
loesung: **Yes.** The total amount of meat remains limited to 1 to 5 %, and it must additionally be beef; every embodiment also falls within the granted claim (Art. 123(3) EPC, Art. 69 EPC).
einheit:e01n123-4b.merke: Genuine limitation: additional feature, old limit remains.
einheit:e01n123-4b.abschnitt: Art. 123(3) EPC: extent of protection after grant

einheit:e01n123-4c.frage: May Y, in opposition, amend "Additive S" to "Use of S for preserving foodstuffs"?
loesung: **Yes.** Changing from a product claim to a claim to the use of the product for a particular purpose does not extend the protection conferred (G 2/88). The reverse, from use to product, would be unallowable.
einheit:e01n123-4c.abwandlung: Another patent of Y claims "Additive S"; it has been opposed.
einheit:e01n123-4c.abschnitt: Art. 123(3) EPC: extent of protection after grant

gruppe:e01n123-5.sachverhalt: During examination, Z added the feature "plastic housing" to claim 1; the application only mentioned a polyamide housing. The patent is granted. An opponent relies on Art. 100(c) EPC.

einheit:e01n123-5a.frage: Can the patent be maintained unamended?
loesung: **No.** "Plastic" goes beyond the original disclosure (Art. 123(2) EPC); the ground for opposition under Art. 100(c) EPC prejudices maintenance (G 1/93).
einheit:e01n123-5a.merke: Added matter in the granted claim: ground for opposition.

einheit:e01n123-5b.frage: Can Z simply delete the feature?
loesung: **No.** Deleting the limiting feature would extend the protection conferred (Art. 123(3) EPC). This is the G 1/93 trap.
einheit:e01n123-5b.merke: Deleting infringes Art. 123(3) EPC, keeping infringes Art. 123(2) EPC.

loesung: **Yes.** Polyamide is originally disclosed and narrower than plastic. If the application provides a basis for the replacement and the protection conferred is not extended, the patent can be maintained (G 1/93; Guidelines H-IV, 3.5).
einheit:e01n123-5c.merke: Way out: replace with a disclosed, narrower feature.

einheit:e01n123-5d.frage: Can the patent be maintained with this feature?
loesung: **Yes.** An undisclosed feature which makes no technical contribution and merely excludes protection for part of the subject-matter is not added matter (G 1/93, headnote 2).
einheit:e01n123-5d.merke: Without a technical contribution, the feature does no harm.
einheit:e01n123-5d.abwandlung: The added feature makes no technical contribution to the invention and merely excludes part of the originally claimed subject-matter from protection.

kapitel:e01n139.titel: R. 139 and 140 EPC: correction of errors

einheit:e01n139-0.text: R. 139 EPC allows linguistic errors, errors of transcription and mistakes in documents filed to be corrected. In the description, claims and drawings, the correction must be **obvious**: error and correction must be derivable from the documents as filed themselves, not from the priority document (G 3/89, G 11/91). Paper D asks about this for translation errors (2015 Question 4), errors in the text under R. 71(3) EPC (2022 Question 2) and the wrong name in the notice of appeal (2023 Question 4, G 1/12). R. 140 EPC concerns decisions only, never the text of the granted patent (G 1/10).

gruppe:e01n139-1.sachverhalt: AA files EP-1 in Japanese with an English translation and EP-2 in English; both claim a Japanese priority. The translation of EP-1 and EP-2 read "©" instead of "µm". The Japanese text of EP-1 and the priority document correctly read "µm"; the context of the English text does not reveal the correction.

einheit:e01n139-1a.frage: Can AA remedy the error in the translation of EP-1?
loesung: **Yes.** Throughout the proceedings, the translation may be brought into conformity with the application as filed, here the Japanese text (second sentence of Art. 14(2) EPC). Obviousness does not matter.
einheit:e01n139-1a.merke: The yardstick for translation errors is the original, not R. 139 EPC.
einheit:e01n139-1a.abschnitt: Second sentence of R. 139 EPC: description, claims, drawings

einheit:e01n139-1b.frage: Can AA correct the error in EP-2 under R. 139 EPC?
loesung: **No.** Error and correction must be immediately evident from the documents as filed (second sentence of R. 139 EPC). The priority document may not be used for this purpose (G 3/89, G 11/91; Guidelines H-VI, 2.2.1).
einheit:e01n139-1b.merke: The priority document does not prove an obvious mistake.
einheit:e01n139-1b.abschnitt: Second sentence of R. 139 EPC: description, claims, drawings

einheit:e01n139-1c.frage: Can AA then correct the error in EP-2?
loesung: **Yes.** If the skilled person recognises from the application itself that there is an error and that only "µm" can be meant, the correction is allowable. It is of a declaratory nature and does not infringe Art. 123(2) EPC (G 3/89).
einheit:e01n139-1c.merke: Error and correction evident from the application itself: correctable.
einheit:e01n139-1c.abwandlung: Tables and dimensions in EP-2 clearly show that only "µm" can be meant.
einheit:e01n139-1c.abschnitt: Second sentence of R. 139 EPC: description, claims, drawings

gruppe:e01n139-2.titel: The typing error in the text for grant
gruppe:e01n139-2.sachverhalt: BB receives a communication under R. 71(3) EPC dated 14 September 2026. Claim 4 reads "polyetylene"; it is obvious that "polyethylene" is meant.

einheit:e01n139-2a.frage: Can BB have the error corrected before grant?
loesung: **Yes.** Within the four-month period, BB files a reasoned request for correction (R. 71(6) EPC, second sentence of R. 139 EPC). If the Examining Division agrees, it issues a new communication under R. 71(3) EPC (Guidelines C-V, 4.3).
einheit:e01n139-2a.merke: Error in the text for grant: object before grant.
einheit:e01n139-2a.abschnitt: R. 139 and 140 EPC: before and after grant

einheit:e01n139-2b.frage: Can BB have the wording of the granted patent corrected under R. 140 EPC?
loesung: **No.** R. 140 EPC is not available for correcting the text of a patent; such a request by the proprietor is inadmissible at any time, including in opposition (G 1/10). The applicant bears responsibility for the approved text.
einheit:e01n139-2b.merke: R. 140 EPC does not cure errors in the approved text.
einheit:e01n139-2b.abwandlung: BB overlooks the error, approves the text, and the patent is granted.
einheit:e01n139-2b.abschnitt: R. 139 and 140 EPC: before and after grant

loesung: **Yes.** If the published specification differs from the Druckexemplar on which the grant is based, there is an error in publication; it can be corrected at any time (Guidelines H-VI, 6).
einheit:e01n139-2c.merke: Printing error in the publication: correctable at any time.
einheit:e01n139-2c.abwandlung: Unlike in the main case, the approved Druckexemplar was error-free; only the published specification contains "polyetylene".
einheit:e01n139-2c.abschnitt: R. 139 and 140 EPC: before and after grant

einheit:e01n139-2d.frage: Can a typing error in the proprietor's name in the decision to grant be corrected under R. 140 EPC?
loesung: **Yes.** Bibliographic data in the decision to grant which obviously do not reflect the Examining Division's intention can be corrected under R. 140 EPC, provided no other person is designated (Guidelines H-VI, 3.2).
einheit:e01n139-2d.merke: R. 140 EPC: errors in decisions, such as bibliographic data.
einheit:e01n139-2d.abschnitt: R. 139 and 140 EPC: before and after grant

gruppe:e01n139-3.sachverhalt: The patent was transferred from CC-AG to DD-GmbH; the transfer has been registered. The Opposition Division revokes the patent. The representative files an appeal in time but mistakenly names CC-AG as appellant; he had been instructed by DD-GmbH.

loesung: **No.** Only a party to the proceedings adversely affected by the decision may appeal (Art. 107 EPC). After the registered transfer, CC-AG is no longer a party.
einheit:e01n139-3a.merke: Only an adversely affected party is entitled to appeal.
einheit:e01n139-3a.abschnitt: First sentence of R. 139 EPC: procedural declarations

einheit:e01n139-3b.frage: Can the appellant's name be corrected to DD-GmbH?
loesung: **Yes.** If the true intention was to file the appeal on behalf of DD-GmbH, the name can be corrected under R. 101(2) EPC and the first sentence of R. 139 EPC. The principle of free evaluation of evidence applies; DD-GmbH's instructions are the evidence (G 1/12).
einheit:e01n139-3b.merke: Wrong name in the notice of appeal: correctable if the intention can be proven.
einheit:e01n139-3b.abschnitt: First sentence of R. 139 EPC: procedural declarations

einheit:e01n139-3c.frage: Can the name be corrected in this case too?
loesung: **No.** The correction must express what was actually intended when the appeal was filed. A later change of mind does not turn the original statement into an error (G 1/12).
einheit:e01n139-3c.merke: A mistake is corrected, not a change of mind.
einheit:e01n139-3c.abwandlung: CC-AG deliberately wanted to file the appeal itself; only later is DD-GmbH to become the appellant.
einheit:e01n139-3c.abschnitt: First sentence of R. 139 EPC: procedural declarations

gruppe:e01n139-4.sachverhalt: On 5 May 2025, EE files a European application for features A and B, claiming priority from P2 of 2 September 2024, which discloses B. EE forgets to indicate the earlier application P1 of 6 May 2024, which discloses A.

einheit:e01n139-4a.frage: Can EE still add the priority of P1 in July 2025?
loesung: **Yes.** The declaration of priority may be made within 16 months of the earliest priority date claimed (R. 52(2) EPC); if the new priority changes that date, the period is calculated from P1 (Guidelines A-III, 6.5.1).
einheit:e01n139-4a.merke: Adding a priority: R. 52(2) EPC, not R. 139 EPC.
einheit:e01n139-4a.abschnitt: First sentence of R. 139 EPC: priority data

einheit:e01n139-4b.frage: Can EE still have P1 inserted under R. 139 EPC now?
loesung: **No,** as a rule not: once the time limits under R. 52 EPC have expired and the application has been published, the EPO protects the public's legitimate expectations. An exception applies only if the error is apparent from the published application itself (J 6/91; Guidelines A-V, 3).
einheit:e01n139-4b.merke: After publication: correction of priority only for an apparent error.
einheit:e01n139-4b.abwandlung: EE notices the omission only in April 2026, after publication; the application does not reveal the error.
einheit:e01n139-4b.abschnitt: First sentence of R. 139 EPC: priority data

kapitel:e01n133.titel: Art. 133 and 134 EPC, R. 151 and 152 EPC: representation

einheit:e01n133-0.text: In Paper D, representation issues arise in facts involving parties outside Europe: 2017 (US acquirer of the patent in opposition), 2018 (Argentinian inventor files himself) and 2024 (joint opposition with an opponent in Mexico). No one is compelled to be represented (Art. 133(1) EPC), except those having **neither residence nor principal place of business** in a Contracting State (Art. 133(2) EPC); nationality does not count. Anyone may file the application himself. Employees act for their employer (Art. 133(3) EPC), legal practitioners under Art. 134(8) EPC. Several parties act through a common representative (R. 151 EPC); if a required authorisation is missing, acts are deemed not to have been taken (R. 152(6) EPC).

gruppe:e01n133-1.sachverhalt: S lives in Brazil. He files the European application EP-S online himself and pays the filing and search fees from his account. The EPO invites him to appoint a professional representative.

einheit:e01n133-1a.frage: Was the filing by S himself effective?
loesung: **Yes.** Art. 133(2) EPC exempts the filing of the application from the obligation to be represented. This covers all acts leading to the accordance of a date of filing (Guidelines A-VIII, 1.1).
einheit:e01n133-1a.abschnitt: Art. 133(2) EPC: obligation to be represented

einheit:e01n133-1b.frage: Was S allowed to pay the fees himself?
loesung: **Yes.** Fees may be validly paid by any person (Guidelines A-X, 1). The obligation to be represented is irrelevant for this.
einheit:e01n133-1b.abschnitt: Art. 133(2) EPC: obligation to be represented

einheit:e01n133-1c.frage: May S reply to the search opinion himself?
loesung: **No.** S must perform all other acts through a professional representative (Art. 133(2) EPC). The EPO treats a submission by S himself like a document not validly signed and invites signature by an entitled person (R. 50(3) EPC; Guidelines A-VIII, 3.1).
einheit:e01n133-1c.merke: After filing, only the representative acts.
einheit:e01n133-1c.abschnitt: Art. 133(2) EPC: obligation to be represented

loesung: **No.** The time limit under R. 58 EPC for appointing a representative is excluded from further processing (R. 135(2) EPC); the application is refused (Art. 90(5) EPC; Guidelines A-III, 16.2).
einheit:e01n133-1d.merke: No representative appointed: refusal without further processing.
einheit:e01n133-1d.abwandlung: S does not appoint a representative within the period set.
einheit:e01n133-1d.abschnitt: Art. 133(2) EPC: obligation to be represented

gruppe:e01n133-2.sachverhalt: T, resident in Italy, and U, an Italian national resident in Canada, file a joint opposition; T is named first. Both sign, and one opposition fee is paid. When invited, U appoints the professional representative V; T appoints no one.

einheit:e01n133-2a.frage: Is one opposition fee sufficient for both?
loesung: **Yes.** An opposition filed in common by several persons is admissible with only one opposition fee (G 3/99).

einheit:e01n133-2b.frage: Did U have to appoint a representative although he is Italian?
loesung: **Yes.** Art. 133(2) EPC refers to residence or principal place of business, not nationality. The representative must also sign or approve the opposition (Guidelines D-IV, 1.2.2.2).

optionen: T, as the person named first
A representative designated by the EPO
loesung: **V.** In principle, the person named first is deemed to be the common representative. However, if one party is obliged to be represented, its professional representative is deemed the common representative unless the person named first has appointed one (R. 151(1) EPC). This also applies to joint opponents.
einheit:e01n133-2c.merke: A mandatory representative displaces an unrepresented first-named party.

einheit:e01n133-2d.frage: Can T later file an appeal against the decision alone?
loesung: **No.** For joint opponents, the common representative must file the appeal. If a non-entitled person files it, it is deemed not duly signed, and the common representative is invited to sign it (G 3/99).
einheit:e01n133-2d.merke: Joint opponents act through the common representative.

gruppe:e01n133-3.sachverhalt: W GmbH, with its principal place of business in Stuttgart, has its application handled by its employed patent engineer X, who is not a professional representative. X replies to a communication without filing an authorisation. W's parent company has its seat in the USA.

loesung: **Yes.** Persons with their principal place of business in a Contracting State may act through an employee, who need not be a professional representative (Art. 133(3) EPC). However, the employee always needs a signed authorisation or the number of a registered general authorisation (Guidelines A-VIII, 1.7).
einheit:e01n133-3a.merke: Employees: no qualification needed, but always an authorisation.
einheit:e01n133-3a.abschnitt: Art. 133(3) EPC, R. 152 EPC: employees and authorisation

einheit:e01n133-3b.frage: X does not file the authorisation within the period set by the EPO either. Does the reply remain effective?
loesung: **No.** If a required authorisation is not filed in due time, any procedural steps taken by the representative other than filing the application are deemed not to have been taken (R. 152(6) EPC). If the time limit for reply has expired, the application is deemed to be withdrawn (Art. 94(4) EPC).
einheit:e01n133-3b.merke: No authorisation: acts deemed not to have been taken.
einheit:e01n133-3b.abschnitt: Art. 133(3) EPC, R. 152 EPC: employees and authorisation

einheit:e01n133-3c.frage: Can X also handle applications of the US parent company?
loesung: **No.** The parent company has no principal place of business in a Contracting State and must act through a professional representative (Art. 133(2) EPC). An employee who is not on the list of professional representatives is not sufficient (Art. 134(1) EPC).
einheit:e01n133-3c.merke: Those obliged to be represented need a professional representative.
einheit:e01n133-3c.abschnitt: Art. 133(3) EPC, R. 152 EPC: employees and authorisation

gruppe:e01n133-4.titel: Change of proprietor before oral proceedings
gruppe:e01n133-4.sachverhalt: The proprietor of the patent is the US company Alpha, represented in opposition proceedings by the professional representative Berg. Alpha transfers the patent to the US company Beta; Berg notifies the EPO of the termination of her authorisation. Written submissions for the oral proceedings may be filed until 7 October 2026.

einheit:e01n133-4a.frage: Can Beta file the amended claims itself?
loesung: **No.** Beta has no principal place of business in a Contracting State and must act through a professional representative (Art. 133(2) EPC). Moreover, the transfer only has effect vis-à-vis the EPO once it is proven by documents (R. 22(3) EPC, R. 85 EPC).
einheit:e01n133-4a.merke: New proprietor outside Europe: appoint a representative, prove the transfer.
einheit:e01n133-4a.abschnitt: Art. 134 EPC, R. 152 EPC: change of representative

einheit:e01n133-4b.frage: May Beta instruct a legal practitioner admitted in Germany instead of a professional representative?
loesung: **Yes.** A legal practitioner qualified in a Contracting State and having his place of business there may act like a professional representative to the extent that he is entitled to act in patent matters in that state (Art. 134(8) EPC). He is not on the list of professional representatives (Guidelines A-VIII, 1.3).
einheit:e01n133-4b.merke: Legal practitioners act within the scope of their national entitlement.
einheit:e01n133-4b.abschnitt: Art. 134 EPC, R. 152 EPC: change of representative

einheit:e01n133-4c.frage: Must the newly appointed professional representative Clausen file a signed authorisation?
loesung: **No,** as a rule not. Professional representatives need file an authorisation only in special cases, such as a change of representative without the previous representative having notified the termination (R. 152(1) EPC; Guidelines A-VIII, 1.7). Berg has notified the termination.
einheit:e01n133-4c.abschnitt: Art. 134 EPC, R. 152 EPC: change of representative

einheit:e01n133-4d.frage: Must Clausen file an authorisation now?
loesung: **Yes.** Where the representative changes without the previous representative having notified the termination, the EPO requires a signed authorisation (Guidelines A-VIII, 1.7). Until such notification, the previous representative is deemed to be authorised (R. 152(8) EPC).
einheit:e01n133-4d.merke: No termination notified: the old representative remains authorised.
einheit:e01n133-4d.abwandlung: Berg had not notified the termination of her authorisation.
einheit:e01n133-4d.abschnitt: Art. 134 EPC, R. 152 EPC: change of representative

kapitel:e01n150.titel: Art. 150 to 152 EPC and PCT: the international phase

einheit:e01n150-0.text: Ten Paper D questions from 2015 to 2025 are set wholly or partly in the international phase (2015 Q3, 2016 Q2, 2017 Q5, 2018 Q1, 2019 Q3, 2021 Q5, 2023 Q2 and Q5, 2024 Q1, 2025 Q5). There, the EPO is receiving Office, International Searching Authority, Authority for supplementary search and International Preliminary Examining Authority (Art. 151 and 152 EPC); the PCT prevails over the EPC (Art. 150(2) EPC). Typical questions: Is the EPO competent as receiving Office? Is the date of filing kept if parts are missing? Until when can a priority be added or restored? Which time limits apply to supplementary search, the demand and amendments?

gruppe:e01n150-1.sachverhalt: Ana, a Portuguese national resident in Brazil, and the Brazilian company Tecno want to file a joint international application in English with the EPO. Ana is also the inventor.

einheit:e01n150-1a.frage: Is the EPO competent as receiving Office?
loesung: **Yes.** It is sufficient that one applicant is a national or resident of an EPC Contracting State (R. 19.1 PCT, R. 157(1) EPC); Ana is Portuguese. The application is also in English (R. 157(2) EPC; PCT-EPO Guidelines A-II, 2).
einheit:e01n150-1a.merke: One applicant from an EPC state is sufficient.
einheit:e01n150-1a.abschnitt: Art. 151 EPC: the EPO as receiving Office

einheit:e01n150-1b.frage: Does the EPO remain competent if the application is filed in Portuguese?
loesung: **No.** As receiving Office, the EPO only accepts English, French or German (R. 157(2) EPC). It transmits the application to the International Bureau as receiving Office; the date of receipt by the EPO counts as the date of receipt (R. 19.4 PCT).
einheit:e01n150-1b.merke: Wrong language: transmittal to the International Bureau, date kept.
einheit:e01n150-1b.abschnitt: Art. 151 EPC: the EPO as receiving Office

einheit:e01n150-1c.frage: Is the EPO now competent as receiving Office?
loesung: **No.** A person named only as inventor is not an applicant; their nationality does not count (PCT-EPO Guidelines A-II, 2). Tecno is neither a national nor a resident of an EPC state. The EPO transmits the application to the International Bureau (R. 19.4 PCT).
einheit:e01n150-1c.merke: The inventor alone does not establish competence.
einheit:e01n150-1c.abwandlung: Ana is named in the request only as inventor; Tecno alone is the applicant.
einheit:e01n150-1c.abschnitt: Art. 151 EPC: the EPO as receiving Office

gruppe:e01n150-2.sachverhalt: On the last day of the priority year, F files the international application PCT-F with the EPO on form PCT/RO/101, claiming priority from the French application FR-F. A week later, F notices that the second page of the claims is missing. FR-F contains it word for word.

einheit:e01n150-2a.frage: Can F file the page later without losing the date of filing?
loesung: **Yes,** by incorporation by reference: the form contains the statement under R. 4.18 PCT, and the missing part is completely contained in FR-F. If F confirms the incorporation in time (R. 20.6 PCT), the date of filing is kept (PCT-EPO Guidelines A-II, 5).
einheit:e01n150-2a.merke: Missing part in the priority document: incorporation without loss of date.
einheit:e01n150-2a.abschnitt: Art. 11 PCT: date of filing and missing parts

einheit:e01n150-2b.frage: Does the date of filing change if the later-filed part is not contained in FR-F?
loesung: **Yes.** Without a basis in the priority document, F can only file missing parts under R. 20.5 PCT; the date of filing then becomes the date of their receipt (PCT-EPO Guidelines A-II, 5). Here, that date falls after the end of the priority year.
einheit:e01n150-2b.merke: Without a basis in the priority, the date of filing moves.
einheit:e01n150-2b.abschnitt: Art. 11 PCT: date of filing and missing parts

einheit:e01n150-2c.frage: Can F have an obvious typing error in claim 3 rectified?
loesung: **Yes,** under R. 91.1 PCT, if error and rectification are obvious to the skilled person. For the description, claims and drawings the searching or examining authority decides, for the request the receiving Office; the request must be submitted within 26 months of the priority date (PCT-EPO Guidelines H-IV, 2.1 and 2.2).
einheit:e01n150-2c.abschnitt: Art. 11 PCT: date of filing and missing parts

einheit:e01n150-2d.frage: Can F nevertheless keep the original date of receipt as the date of filing?
loesung: **Yes.** Without claims, a requirement of Art. 11 PCT is missing. However, an entire element can also be incorporated by reference if it is completely contained in the priority document and F confirms this in time (R. 20.6 PCT). Unlike under R. 40(1) EPC, the PCT date of filing requires claims.
einheit:e01n150-2d.merke: PCT: no claims, no date of filing, unless by reference.
einheit:e01n150-2d.abwandlung: F has filed no claims at all.
einheit:e01n150-2d.abschnitt: Art. 11 PCT: date of filing and missing parts

gruppe:e01n150-3.sachverhalt: On Saturday, 8 March 2025, G electronically files the French application FR2, and on 20 March 2025 FR1. On Monday, 9 March 2026, G files the international application PCT-G with the EPO, claiming only FR1. G has forgotten FR2.

einheit:e01n150-3a.frage: Is PCT-G still within the priority year for FR2?
loesung: **Yes.** The priority year ended on Sunday, 8 March 2026. If the Office is closed on that day, the period is extended to the next day on which it is open (R. 80.5 PCT; PCT-EPO Guidelines A-VI, 1.2).
einheit:e01n150-3a.merke: Period ending at the weekend: next working day, also for the priority year.

einheit:e01n150-3b.frage: Until when can G add the priority claim for FR2?
loesung: **By 9 July 2026.** The period is 16 months from the priority date; if that date changes, whichever period expires first applies, here 16 months from FR2 (8 July 2026). In any event, however, four months from the international filing date suffice (R. 26bis.1 PCT; PCT-EPO Guidelines A-VI, 1.4.1).
einheit:e01n150-3b.merke: Adding: 16 months, at least four months from the filing date.

einheit:e01n150-3c.frage: By when must G then enter the European phase?
loesung: **By 8 October 2027.** The 31 months are calculated from the earliest priority date (R. 159(1) EPC), so after the addition from FR2. 8 October 2027 is a Friday.
einheit:e01n150-3c.merke: New earlier priority, earlier entry deadline.

gruppe:e01n150-4.sachverhalt: On 10 June 2025, H files the US application US-H. Owing to an isolated mistake by an experienced assistant in an otherwise reliable time-limit monitoring system, the international application PCT-H claiming that priority only reaches the EPO as receiving Office on 15 June 2026.

einheit:e01n150-4a.frage: Is the priority claim void in the international phase?
loesung: **No.** PCT-H was received within two months of expiry of the priority year (10 June 2026). The claim is not considered void in the international phase and remains the basis for calculating time limits (R. 26bis.2 PCT; PCT-EPO Guidelines A-VI, 1.5).
einheit:e01n150-4a.merke: Up to two months late: priority remains for time limits.
einheit:e01n150-4a.abschnitt: R. 26bis.3 PCT: restoration of the right of priority

einheit:e01n150-4b.frage: Can H obtain restoration from the EPO as receiving Office?
loesung: **Yes.** Request with reasons and fee within two months of expiry of the priority year, i.e. by 10 August 2026 (R. 26bis.3 PCT). The EPO applies only the due care criterion, as under Art. 122 EPC; an isolated mistake in an otherwise reliable system suffices (PCT-EPO Guidelines A-VI, 1.5).
einheit:e01n150-4b.merke: EPO as receiving Office: restoration only with due care.
einheit:e01n150-4b.abschnitt: R. 26bis.3 PCT: restoration of the right of priority

einheit:e01n150-4c.frage: Must H request restoration again on entry into the European phase?
loesung: **No.** If the EPO as receiving Office restores the priority under the due care criterion, this also has effect before the EPO as designated Office (R. 49ter.1 PCT; Guidelines A-XV, 5).
einheit:e01n150-4c.merke: Due care criterion at the receiving Office: binds the EPO as designated Office.
einheit:e01n150-4c.abschnitt: R. 26bis.3 PCT: restoration of the right of priority

einheit:e01n150-4d.frage: Does this restoration have effect before the EPO?
loesung: **No.** The EPO recognises only restorations under the due care criterion. H must file a new reasoned request with the EPO as designated Office within one month of expiry of the 31-month time limit and pay the fee (R. 49ter.2 PCT; Guidelines A-XV, 5).
einheit:e01n150-4d.merke: "Unintentional" is not enough for the EPO.
einheit:e01n150-4d.abwandlung: H files PCT-H with the US Office, which restores the priority only under the unintentionality criterion.
einheit:e01n150-4d.abschnitt: R. 26bis.3 PCT: restoration of the right of priority

gruppe:e01n150-5.titel: Invention D is to be examined
gruppe:e01n150-5.sachverhalt: On 4 August 2025, I files the international application PCT-I in English, without priority, with the Swedish Office, which is also the International Searching Authority. PCT-I claims the non-unitary inventions C and D. The Swedish Office searches only C because I pays no additional fee. I wants D to be examined by the EPO.

einheit:e01n150-5a.frage: Can the EPO as International Preliminary Examining Authority examine D although D has not been searched?
loesung: **No.** The EPO as International Preliminary Examining Authority does not examine claims for which no search has been carried out (R. 66.1 PCT; PCT-EPO Guidelines C-IV, 1.1). The EPO would be competent because the Swedish Office carried out the search (PCT-EPO Guidelines C-II, 2).
einheit:e01n150-5a.abschnitt: R. 45bis and 54bis PCT: supplementary search, preliminary examination, amendments

einheit:e01n150-5b.frage: By when can I request a supplementary international search on D by the EPO from the International Bureau?
loesung: **By 4 June 2027.** The request must be made within 22 months of the priority date, here the date of filing (R. 45bis.1 PCT). I indicates that D is to be searched; the EPO follows this if it takes the same view on lack of unity (PCT-EPO Guidelines B-XII, 10.3).
einheit:e01n150-5b.merke: Supplementary search: 22 months, at the International Bureau.
einheit:e01n150-5b.abschnitt: R. 45bis and 54bis PCT: supplementary search, preliminary examination, amendments

einheit:e01n150-5c.frage: Can I also amend the description with amendments under Art. 19 PCT?
loesung: **No.** After receipt of the search report, Art. 19 PCT allows only amendments of the claims, filed with the International Bureau. The description and drawings can only be amended in preliminary examination under Art. 34 PCT (PCT-EPO Guidelines H-I, 3).
einheit:e01n150-5c.merke: Art. 19 PCT: claims only; Art. 34 PCT: everything.
einheit:e01n150-5c.abschnitt: R. 45bis and 54bis PCT: supplementary search, preliminary examination, amendments

einheit:e01n150-5d.frage: Must I file the demand no later than 22 months from the priority date?
loesung: **No,** not necessarily: the decisive period is whichever of two periods expires later, three months from transmittal of the search report or 22 months from the priority date (R. 54bis.1 PCT). A late demand is considered not to have been submitted (PCT-EPO Guidelines C-II, 1.1).
einheit:e01n150-5d.merke: Demand: the period expiring later counts.
einheit:e01n150-5d.abschnitt: R. 45bis and 54bis PCT: supplementary search, preliminary examination, amendments

kapitel:e01n153.titel: Art. 153 EPC, R. 159 to 165 EPC: Euro-PCT

einheit:e01n153-0.text: Entry of a PCT application into the European phase is core Paper D material (2016 Q3, 2017 Q1, 2021 Q2, 2022 Q3, 2025 Q1). An international application with a date of filing is equivalent to a European application (Art. 153(2) EPC). However, it is only processed once the applicant performs the acts under R. 159(1) EPC within **31 months** of the earliest priority date, or earlier upon express request (Art. 23(2) PCT). Further processing cures failures (R. 160 EPC). After entry, R. 161 and 162 EPC follow, and R. 164 EPC in the case of lack of unity. A divisional application requires effective entry (J 18/09).

gruppe:e01n153-1.sachverhalt: On 9 April 2025, K files a Japanese application and, on 7 April 2026, claiming its priority, the international application PCT-K in Japanese with the Japan Patent Office. PCT-K is published in Japanese. K wants a European patent.

einheit:e01n153-1a.frage: By when must K perform the acts under R. 159(1) EPC?
loesung: **By 9 November 2027.** The time limit is 31 months from the priority date, not from the international filing date (R. 159(1) EPC, R. 131(4) EPC). 9 November 2027 is a Tuesday.
einheit:e01n153-1a.merke: 31 months from the earliest priority date.
einheit:e01n153-1a.abschnitt: R. 159(1) EPC and R. 160 EPC: entry and failure to act

loesung: **Yes.** PCT-K was not published in an official language of the EPO. K must file a translation into English, French or German (Art. 153(4) EPC, R. 159(1)(a) EPC); that language becomes the language of the proceedings. In addition, K pays the fees due and files the request for examination (R. 159(1) EPC).
einheit:e01n153-1b.merke: Not published in an official language: translation within 31 months.
einheit:e01n153-1b.abschnitt: R. 159(1) EPC and R. 160 EPC: entry and failure to act

einheit:e01n153-1c.frage: K lets the time limit expire; the EPO notifies K that the application is deemed to be withdrawn. Can K remedy this?
loesung: **Yes,** with further processing: within two months of the communication (R. 160(2) EPC, R. 112(1) EPC), pay the fee for further processing and complete the translation, fees and request for examination (Art. 121 EPC, R. 135(1) EPC; Guidelines A-XIII, 3.3).
einheit:e01n153-1c.abschnitt: R. 159(1) EPC and R. 160 EPC: entry and failure to act

einheit:e01n153-1d.frage: K pays only the filing fee and never files a translation. Is PCT-K an earlier right under Art. 54(3) EPC against later European applications?
loesung: **No.** A Euro-PCT application is considered state of the art under Art. 54(3) EPC only if the translation under Art. 153(4) EPC has been filed **and** the filing fee has been paid (Art. 153(5) EPC, R. 165 EPC). With a Japanese publication, payment alone is not enough.
einheit:e01n153-1d.merke: R. 165 EPC: translation and filing fee.
einheit:e01n153-1d.abschnitt: R. 159(1) EPC and R. 160 EPC: entry and failure to act

gruppe:e01n153-2.sachverhalt: On 3 February 2025, R files the international application PCT-R in Russian, without priority, with the Russian Office; it is published in Russian with the search report on 13 August 2026. On 15 October 2026, R expressly requests immediate processing from the EPO and pays the filing and search fees.

einheit:e01n153-2a.frage: Is the request of 15 October 2026 effective?
loesung: **No.** Early processing (Art. 23(2) and 40(2) PCT) only takes effect once the requirements of R. 159(1) EPC are met as if the 31-month time limit expired on that day. The translation under Art. 153(4) EPC is always required; it is missing (Guidelines A-XII, 7.1).
einheit:e01n153-2a.merke: Early processing: translation, filing fee and, where applicable, search fee always.

einheit:e01n153-2b.frage: Must R also file the request for examination at the same time?
loesung: **No,** not on 15 October 2026: the time limit under R. 70(1) EPC is still running; it ends six months after publication of the international search report (Art. 153(6) EPC). The request for examination, designation fee and renewal fee are required only if their time limits have already expired (R. 159(1) EPC; Guidelines A-XII, 7.1).
einheit:e01n153-2b.merke: Only time limits already expired must be met immediately.

einheit:e01n153-2c.frage: Can R file a divisional application from that day?
loesung: **Yes.** With effective early processing, the application is pending before the EPO; from that day, a divisional application is possible (Guidelines A-XIII, 9.1.2). Before effective entry, it is not (J 18/09).
einheit:e01n153-2c.merke: Divisional application only after effective entry.
einheit:e01n153-2c.abwandlung: R files the translation later; the request becomes effective.

gruppe:e01n153-3.sachverhalt: U files PCT-U with the EPO as receiving Office. The EPO as International Searching Authority considers inventions X and Y to lack unity; U pays no additional search fee, and only X is searched. On entry into the European phase, U directs the claims only to Y.

einheit:e01n153-3a.frage: Does the EPO draw up a supplementary European search report?
loesung: **No.** Where the EPO was the International Searching Authority, no supplementary European search report is drawn up (Art. 153(7) EPC; Guidelines B-II, 4.3.1). No search fee under R. 159(1)(e) EPC is payable.
einheit:e01n153-3a.merke: EPO as ISA: no supplementary European search.

einheit:e01n153-3b.frage: Does the Examining Division examine Y without a further fee?
loesung: **No.** There is no EPO search for Y. The Examining Division invites U to pay a search fee for Y within two months (R. 164(2)(a) EPC). If U pays, Y is searched and examined; otherwise U must limit the application to X (R. 164(2) EPC).
einheit:e01n153-3b.merke: Unsearched invention: fee under R. 164(2) EPC.

einheit:e01n153-3c.frage: Can U still pursue Y if he does not pay the fee?
loesung: **Yes,** with a divisional application (Art. 76 EPC) while the Euro-PCT application is pending; there, Y is searched against a separate search fee. The Euro-PCT application itself remains limited to X.
einheit:e01n153-3c.merke: Lack of unity: divisional application for the rest.

einheit:e01n153-3d.titel: EPO as Authority for supplementary search
einheit:e01n153-3d.frage: Does the same then apply to Y?
loesung: **Yes.** After a supplementary international search by the EPO, too, no supplementary European search report is drawn up (Guidelines B-II, 4.3.1). R. 164(2) EPC expressly also covers inventions not searched by the EPO as Authority for supplementary search.
einheit:e01n153-3d.merke: EPO as SISA is treated like the EPO as ISA.
einheit:e01n153-3d.abwandlung: The International Searching Authority was the Chinese Office; the EPO, as Authority for supplementary search, searched only X.

gruppe:e01n153-4.sachverhalt: V files PCT-V in English with the EPO; the EPO as International Searching Authority denies novelty in the written opinion. V enters the European phase with 22 claims and pays no claims fees. The EPO issues the communication under R. 161(1) and 162 EPC.

einheit:e01n153-4a.frage: Must V react to the written opinion?
loesung: **Yes.** If the EPO as International Searching Authority has identified deficiencies, V must comment or amend within six months of the communication. If he does neither, the application is deemed to be withdrawn (R. 161(1) EPC); further processing is available against this.
einheit:e01n153-4a.merke: Negative WO-ISA of the EPO: mandatory reply within six months.

einheit:e01n153-4b.frage: Must V pay claims fees for seven claims if, within the six-month period, he limits the application to 15 claims?
loesung: **No.** Unpaid claims fees can still be paid within the period under R. 161(1) EPC; if V files amended claims within it, the fees are computed on the basis of those claims (R. 162(2) EPC). With 15 claims, none are payable. Unpaid fees count as abandonment of the claim (R. 162(4) EPC).
einheit:e01n153-4b.merke: Claims fees based on the claims at the end of the six-month period.

einheit:e01n153-4c.frage: Can V file a French translation on entry so that the proceedings are conducted in French?
loesung: **No.** PCT-V was published in English; English is the language of the proceedings. A translation into another official language is not provided for (G 4/08; Art. 14(3) EPC).
einheit:e01n153-4c.merke: Published in an official language: that language remains.

gruppe:e01n153-5.sachverhalt: On 12 November 2024, B files the European application EP-B. On 12 November 2025, the German nationals A and B jointly file PCT-AB with the EPO, claiming the priority of EP-B. On 2 March 2026, they want to postpone entry into the European phase for as long as possible.

einheit:e01n153-5a.frage: Can A and B postpone entry by withdrawing the priority claim?
loesung: **Yes.** Withdrawal is possible up to 30 months from the priority date (R. 90bis.3 PCT). Time limits not yet expired are then computed from the new priority date, here the date of filing: the 31-month time limit (R. 159(1) EPC) only ends on 12 June 2028 instead of in June 2027 (PCT-EPO Guidelines A-IV, 2.4).
einheit:e01n153-5a.merke: Withdrawing the priority postpones all open time limits.
einheit:e01n153-5a.abschnitt: Art. 153 EPC: priority and time of entry

einheit:e01n153-5b.frage: Is it sufficient for B alone to declare the withdrawal?
loesung: **No.** The withdrawal must be signed by all applicants, or by an appointed agent or common representative. The merely deemed common representative (the first-named applicant) is not sufficient (R. 90bis.5 PCT; PCT-EPO Guidelines A-IV, 2.1).
einheit:e01n153-5b.abschnitt: Art. 153 EPC: priority and time of entry

einheit:e01n153-5c.frage: Can EP-B be prejudicial to the Euro-PCT application after withdrawal of the priority?
loesung: **Yes.** EP-B is published around May 2026 and is then state of the art under Art. 54(3) EPC against PCT-AB, whose relevant date is now 12 November 2025. B should withdraw EP-B before completion of the technical preparations for publication.
einheit:e01n153-5c.merke: Without priority, one's own first application becomes an earlier right.
einheit:e01n153-5c.abschnitt: Art. 153 EPC: priority and time of entry

einheit:e01n153-5d.frage: Does the withdrawal of the priority then still have effect for the European phase?
loesung: **No.** With effective early processing, the international phase ends vis-à-vis the EPO; a later withdrawal under R. 90bis PCT has no effect there (R. 90bis.6 PCT; Guidelines A-XII, 7.1).
einheit:e01n153-5d.merke: After effective entry, PCT withdrawals no longer help in Europe.
einheit:e01n153-5d.abwandlung: A and B had previously effectively requested early processing from the EPO.
einheit:e01n153-5d.abschnitt: Art. 153 EPC: priority and time of entry
